title: Associate Claims Inspector
description:
This role is designed as a developmental entry point into homeowner claims adjusting at Plymouth Rock. You will begin by conducting on-site property inspections, documenting damage, taking measurements, and communicating your findings to the handling adjuster. For a candidate who demonstrates strong performance, excellent time management, professionalism and empathy with policyholders, and a clear desire to learn homeowner claims adjusting, there may be an opportunity to be considered for a permanent role.

This position requires regular field travel within approximately one to two hours of your home. Because you will often meet policyholders during stressful circumstances, clear communication, professionalism, empathy, reliability, and good judgment are essential.

  • This is a contractor position with the potential to transition to a permanent role based on demonstrated performance, readiness, business needs, and available opportunities.
  • Plymouth Rock will provide basic equipment needed for the assignment.
  • The contractor is responsible for maintaining reliable transportation for required field travel.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct on-site inspections at insured properties and represent Plymouth Rock professionally in every policyholder interaction.
  • Capture thorough, high-quality photo documentation of reported and visible damage to the structure, roofing, siding, interior, and personal property, as applicable.
  • Take accurate measurements and field notes needed by the handling adjuster to scope and evaluate the loss.
  • Communicate inspection findings clearly and promptly using company-approved tools and documentation standards.
  • Set appropriate expectations with policyholders regarding the inspection process, next steps, and adjuster follow-up.
  • Coordinate with approved vendors for mitigation or temporary repairs when directed by the handling adjuster.
  • Identify and flag potential subrogation sources or liability exposures observed during an inspection.
  • Manage a daily field schedule effectively and complete inspections and documentation within required timeframes.
  • Maintain a professional, empathetic, service-focused approach with policyholders throughout every interaction.

Travel expectations vary, but candidates should expect to routinely travel one to two hours from home on a daily basis.

Development Opportunity

This assignment is intended for someone who wants to build a career in homeowner claims. Candidates who demonstrate the skills, judgment, reliability, and learning mindset needed for claims adjusting may be considered for transition to a permanent claims role as business needs and opportunities allow.

  • Build foundational knowledge of property construction, damage indicators, claim documentation, and policyholder communication.
  • Learn the fundamentals of estimate writing, coverage application, reserving, and scope-of-loss documentation.
  • Develop toward greater ownership of homeowner property claims, including investigation, evaluation, estimating, and settlement.

Qualifications

  • Excellent time-management and organizational skills, with the ability to independently manage a field schedule and meet documentation deadlines.
  • Professional, empathetic, and clear communication with policyholders, particularly during stressful situations.
  • A demonstrated desire to learn homeowner claims adjusting and grow your knowledge of property claims.
  • Strong observational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to identify and document relevant damage indicators.
  • Ability to multitask, adapt quickly, follow direction, and apply feedback in a field environment.
  • Construction, mitigation, remediation, property inspection, or related experience is preferred but not required.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and mobile technology.
  • Ability to carry up to 25 lbs. and conduct roof inspections on homes under two stories.
  • A valid driver's license and proficient driving record.
  • Reliable transportation for regular travel to policyholder properties and other assigned field locations.

Salary Range: $50,000 - $67,000 a year. Actual compensation will vary based on multiple factors, including employee knowledge and experience, role scope, business needs, geographical location, and internal equity.

About the Company

The Plymouth Rock Company and its affiliated group of companies write and manage over $2 billion in personal and commercial auto and homeowner’s insurance throughout the Northeast and mid-Atlantic, where we have built an unparalleled reputation for service. We continuously invest in technology, our employees thrive in our empowering environment, and our customers are among the most loyal in the industry. The Plymouth Rock group of companies employs more than 1,900 people and is headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. Plymouth Rock Assurance Corporation holds an A.M. Best rating of “A-/Excellent”

title: Sr Director of Security
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Senior Director of Security provides day-to-day oversight and direction of Constellis’ enterprise security function under the guidance of the Chief Administrative and Security Officer. The role leads industrial security, personnel security, physical security, classified information safeguarding, visitor management, security education, insider threat support, and related compliance programs. The Senior Director translates enterprise risk priorities into operating plans, allocates resources, establishes performance standards, advises senior leaders, and ensures security enables business execution while meeting NISPOM, DCSA, Intelligence Community, DoD, and customer requirements.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Direct day-to-day operations of the enterprise Security Department, including Facility Security Officer, Personnel Security, classified document control, visitor management, physical security, security education, and site-security activities across Constellis locations and programs.
  • Develop and execute the enterprise security operating plan under the Chief Administrative and Security Officer’s guidance, including governance, annual priorities, staffing, succession, budget, technology, service levels, and performance expectations aligned with business objectives and contractual obligations.
  • Lead, develop, and hold accountable FSOs, Personnel Security Specialists, and other security personnel; establish clear decision rights, workload priorities, service standards, professional development plans, and escalation protocols.
  • Own enterprise compliance with 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM), DCSA requirements, applicable Intelligence Community Directives, DoD requirements, Executive Orders, and customer-specific security obligations across facility clearances, personnel security, classified contracts, and classified information safeguarding.
  • Oversee personnel security operations, including clearance lifecycle management, investigations, reinvestigations, onboarding, offboarding, DISS/NBIS recordkeeping, clearance rosters, visit requests, briefings, debriefings, and training records.
  • Oversee classified program support, classified document accountability, classified storage, receipt and transmission, marking reviews, destruction records, inventories, courier program requirements, security containers, and safeguarding of classified information.
  • Establish a repeatable security-risk assessment process for facilities, programs, and business changes; prioritize mitigations based on threat, vulnerability, mission impact, contractual exposure, and cost.
  • Direct physical security standards for corporate and program locations, including access control, alarms, video surveillance, visitor procedures, guard-force interfaces, emergency coordination, and protection of critical assets.
  • Partner with business development, contracts, legal, and integration teams on new pursuits, contract transitions, acquisitions, divestitures, facility openings or closures, and other business changes requiring security due diligence or implementation.

title: Associate Product Manager
description:
The Associate Product Manager will own the P&L and play a key role in shaping, scaling, and driving the profitable growth of a high potential growth state. In this role, you will analyze product performance, develop actionable recommendations, and manage projects that support the growth and profitability of our auto insurance portfolio.

The Associate Product Manager will partner closely with cross-functional teams, including Underwriting, Actuarial, Product Management, Marketing, Claims, Legal, and IT, to execute initiatives that advance business objectives and deliver long-term results. Key responsibilities include evaluating and enhancing product offerings, strengthening underwriting capabilities, and leveraging data-driven insights to solve complex business challenges. Success in this role requires an understanding of market dynamics, competitor activity, and the regulatory landscape. You will independently lead state-specific priorities while collaborating with leadership on broader strategic initiatives and more complex business decisions.

Responsibilities:

title: Project Manager - Marine
description:
The Hiller Companies, LLC has an immediate opening for Project Manager - Marine. If you are a dedicated professional with a passion for fire protection and safety, we invite you to apply today.

The Hiller Companies is a leading provider of fire protection and safety solutions, dedicated to safeguarding lives and property all around the world. Headquartered in Mobile, Alabama, Hiller extends its reach globally as well as in domestic markets with offices across the United States. With over 100 years in the industry, our mission is to ensure the highest standards of safety and innovation in comprehensive fire protection services, including installation, inspection, maintenance, and repair of critical fire and life safety equipment. Our team remains laser-focused on one goal – making the world a safer place.

Job Summary: The primary responsibility of the Project Manager is to bring in each project on or under budget by controlling costs as outlined below and forecasting revenue and costs for the life of the project. The PM will be responsible for coordinating, managing a portfolio and completing multiple concurrent new construction, retrofit, and conversion projects of varying size, on vessels such as OSVs, tugs, barges, towboats, and ferries. The PM is responsible for attending shipyard and owner project meetings, and maintaining accurate records of meetings, yard schedules, vessel availability windows, and owner requests. Responsible for managing the change order process from inception to completion, including owner-directed changes and class-driven revisions. Proactive approach to anticipate and identify problems early, including drydock and delivery schedule pressures, and implement cost effective solutions. Ability to work inter-departmentally with Sales, Engineering, Production Management, Foremen and Technicians. Assures compliance with project closeout requirements, USCG and classification society approvals, SOLAS and flag state requirements, and closeout documentation.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Duties include assisting proposal activities, attendance in pre-bid meetings and owner/shipyard kickoff meetings, vessel walk-downs and condition surveys, selection of subcontractors, maintaining project documentation, and managing materials purchases throughout the lifecycle of the project.
  • Manage project, change orders, man-loading charts, weekly progress reports, material and equipment promise dates for deliveries, completion dates and other elements as required to control the project in accordance with approved budget.
  • Manage rental equipment, staging, and dockside delivery and pick up schedules, including cranes, lifts, and shipyard services, to minimize costs.
  • Develop and maintain project schedule, coordinating installation sequencing with the shipyard master schedule, drydock dates, and other trades.
  • Coordinate submittal of system drawings and calculations to USCG, ABS, DNV, or other classification societies and flag administrations, and maintain a set of as-built and working drawings, consulting with vessel owners, naval architects, engineers, surveyors, and the Authority Having Jurisdiction.
  • Acts as primary interface for vessel owners, operators, and shipyards.
  • Conduct/Attend shipyard and construction meetings, maintain safety program (including hot work permits, confined space entry, and vessel-specific safety requirements), scheduling and change order management, and project close-out documentation.
  • Plan and coordinate system testing and commissioning, including hydrostatic, flow, alarm, and discharge tests, and witness testing with USCG inspectors, class surveyors, and owner representatives through final acceptance, punch list closure, and delivery of the vessel.
  • Perform other duties as business needs dictate and as required.
  • Coordinates and works with field management to manage resources in order to meet shipyard schedules, including testing and delivery dates, as well as budgets.
  • Attend weekly meetings with operations and finance to provide percentage of completion and cost-to-complete updates.

title: Environmental Permitting Project Manager
description:
This Opportunity

WSP is seeking an Environmental Permitting Project Manager to support our Permitting, Planning, and Licensing practice in North Florida (located either in Gainesville or Jacksonville). This role will focus on managing the permitting strategy, environmental compliance, natural resource assessments, and regulatory coordination for a variety of projects within the energy, oil & gas, utilities, transportation, industrial, government, and infrastructure sectors.

The selected candidate will manage permitting and environmental planning projects, working closely with subject matter experts, biologists, environmental planners, engineers, and regulatory specialists. Responsibilities will include developing permitting strategies, preparing regulatory documentation, supporting business development efforts, managing project tasks, and mentoring junior staff. Projects may involve federal, state, and local permitting, natural resource assessments, wetland and waters evaluations, threatened and endangered species coordination, mitigation planning, and environmental compliance support throughout project lifecycles.

We are seeking a candidate who brings strong technical expertise, regulatory knowledge, project management capabilities, and a solution-oriented mindset to help deliver successful projects while contributing to the continued growth of WSP's practice throughout Florida and the southeast.

Your Impact

  • Support and lead environmental permitting and natural resource projects throughout Florida and the southeast.
  • Develop permitting strategies and regulatory pathways for infrastructure, energy, utility, transportation, industrial, and infrastructure projects.
  • Prepare and review permit applications, technical reports, environmental assessments, and supporting documentation.
  • Contribute to staffing plans and manage multidisciplinary teams, teaming partners, and subcontractors to meet project requirements and client commitments.
  • Coordinate with federal, state, and local regulatory agencies to facilitate project approvals.
  • Plan, coordinate, and provide technical oversight for wetland delineations, habitat assessments, threatened and endangered species evaluations, and other natural resource studies.
  • Provide clients with environmental compliance and permitting guidance throughout project development and implementation.
  • Develop project scopes, schedules, budgets, and proposals.
  • Manage multiple projects while ensuring quality deliverables are completed on time and within budget.
  • Analyze and interpret environmental data and provide technical review and quality assurance.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to support environmental reviews, permit applications, mitigation plans, and resource management strategies.
  • Mentor and support the professional development of junior environmental staff.
  • Build and maintain strong client relationships and support business development initiatives; help convert successful project delivery into repeat business.
  • Foster a culture of technical excellence, collaboration, innovation, and exceptional client service.
  • Promote a strong safety culture and maintain compliance with WSP health and safety standards.
  • Exercise sound and ethical decision-making in accordance with WSP policies and procedures.
  • Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.
  • Manage project financial performance, including forecasting, invoicing, change management, risk identification and corrective actions needed to achieve scope, schedule, budget, quality and profitability goals.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in biology, environmental science, natural resources, environmental planning, ecology, geography, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 7 years of experience in natural resources, environmental permitting, environmental consulting, or a related field.
  • Experience supporting projects in Florida and the southeast.
  • Strong understanding of environmental permitting processes and regulatory frameworks, including NEPA, Clean Water Act Sections 404 and 401, Endangered Species Act, and related state regulations.
  • Experience coordinating with agencies such as USACE, USFWS, NOAA, EPA, and Florida and other state regulatory agencies.
  • Knowledge of wetland permitting, habitat assessments, ecological surveys, mitigation planning, and environmental compliance requirements.
  • Demonstrated project management experience, including scope development, budget management, and client communication.
  • Strong technical writing and communication skills with experience preparing reports, permit applications, and presentations.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary consulting environment.
  • Proven commitment to workplace safety and quality project delivery.
  • Ability to travel, including occasional overnight travel for client meetings, agency coordination, and project initiation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in environmental science, biology, ecology, natural resource management, environmental planning, or related field.
  • Previous project management experience in the environmental field.
  • Experience managing multidisciplinary environmental and permitting projects.
  • Experience with large-scale energy, utility, transportation, coastal restoration, or infrastructure projects.
  • Established relationships with regulatory agencies and clients throughout Florida and the southeast.
  • Experience mentoring and developing junior staff.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or similar credential.
  • Professional Wetland Scientist

description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Constellis Finance Rotation Program (FRP) is a two-year, three-rotation program (~8 months per rotation) designed to develop recent college graduates into strong, well-rounded finance professionals who have the financial fluency and business acumen to understand enterprise finance from every angle.   • Program Control: Foundational experience in budgets, forecasting, and financial performance at a project level
  • Business Intelligence & Reporting:Develop dashboards, reporting solutions, and analytical tools that transform data into actionable business insights

  • Identify opportunities to drive efficiency and improve financial processes, reporting, and data quality
  • Complete a capstone project and present your findings to senior finance leadership

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field, with expected graduation between December 2026 and June 2027

title: Senior AWS Cloud Engineer
description:
Senior AWS Cloud Engineer

The Senior AWS Cloud Engineer is a key member of a regionally distributed team (Massachusetts and New Jersey) responsible for designing, implementing, and managing cloud infrastructure solutions on AWS with focus on resiliency, cost effectiveness, and data security. This role emphasizes Infrastructure as Code utilizing Terraform, supporting both proprietary and vendor applications through a growing list of AWS services such as Amazon EKS, Lambda, EC2 Autoscaling RDS and others. The ideal candidate demonstrates advanced expertise in implementing AWS services, Kubernetes, and cloud-native architecture as well as experience with traditional Co-location Data Center Environments.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities:

  • Design, implementation, and management of AWS cloud infrastructure, ensuring high availability, performance, and cost-effective resource allocation.
  • Define and evolve AWS service deployment standards aligned with industry standards.
  • Lead and execute migration initiatives from on-premises infrastructure to AWS including assessment planning and hands-on migration activities.
  • Configure and secure VPCs, subnets, security groups, route tables, VPNs, and related network components for robust connectivity across cloud, internet, and co-location environments.
  • Maintain comprehensive documentation so support organization knowledge and infrastructure maintainability.
  • Work effectively cross functionally across Application development, Infrastructure, Information security, business continuity management to ensure alignment and knowledge sharing.
  • Provide timely updates on assigned task status and completion.
  • Implement monitoring solutions (e.g. AWS CloudWatch) to ensure infrastructure health, performance, and security.
  • Enforce security and compliance standards, including data encryption, access control, and audit logging,
  • Provide technical support and resolution for cloud infrastructure issues during and outside of business hours.

Qualifications and Education:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or related fields and seven (7) years of progressive AWS Cloud Engineering or administration experience. platform.
  • Proven expertise in Terraform code development including complex terraform module development for mission critical deployments.
  • Advanced Python programming skills for automation, orchestration, and integration with AWS services.
  • Proficiency with Docker and Kubernetes, including managing containerized workloads and orchestrating deployments at scale.
  • Familiarity with advanced monitoring and logging tools (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, AWS CloudWatch, CloudTrail) for observability and troubleshooting.
  • Extensive Experience with AWS services (including but not limited to EC2, S3, RDS, Lambda, IAM/IDC, CloudFormation, CloudWatch)

title: Computer Vision and Automation Specialist
description:
Job Summary

We are seeking a driven and innovative Computer Vision & Automation Specialist to join our team in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. This role is ideal for a technology-focused professional who enjoys using automation, computer vision, and data-driven solutions to solve real-world manufacturing challenges and improve safety, quality, and operational efficiency. As a key partner to Engineering and Production teams, you will design, develop, and continuously improve automated manufacturing processes with a strong focus on Computer Vision applications, Python-based solutions, and Manufacturing Digital Transformation (DX) initiatives. You will also apply foundational knowledge of PLC controls to support the effective integration of computer vision and automation technologies with manufacturing equipment and processes.

If you enjoy combining technology, programming, automation, and manufacturing to develop practical solutions, eliminate inefficiencies, and advance smart manufacturing, this is an excellent opportunity to grow your career while making a direct impact on the future of manufacturing operations.

Benefits

  • 401(k) plan with company match
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Earned paid time off (ETO)
  • 10 paid company holidays annually
  • Performance-based merit increases
  • Annual bonus opportunity

Core Responsibilities

Computer Vision & AI Systems Development

  • Lead the development and deployment of computer vision inspection systems for manufacturing and production environments.
  • Design, build, and maintain end-to-end machine vision pipelines using Python and modern ML/CV frameworks such as YOLO, Florence-2, SAM, OpenCV, and PyTorch.
  • Own the full model lifecycle, including data collection, dataset creation, annotation, model training, validation, and performance optimization.
  • Develop custom OCR and defect-detection solutions capable of operating at production-line speed across multi-camera inspection systems.

Manufacturing Automation & System Integration

  • Integrate vision systems with plant automation infrastructure, including PLC communications and manufacturing control systems.
  • Design and implement error-proofing (poka-yoke) solutions utilizing automation, sensing, and machine vision technologies to prevent defects and improve product quality.
  • Support equipment and automation integration by applying knowledge of PLC controls, including Allen-Bradley/Rockwell Automation platforms, tag structures, and ladder logic.
  • Collaborate with engineering, operations, and production teams to identify inspection opportunities and implement scalable technical solutions.

Deployment, Reliability & Operational Support

  • Deploy and maintain applications within containerized environments using Docker and version control systems such as Git.
  • Implement real-time monitoring, alerting, and reporting systems to ensure inspection reliability, uptime, and responsive issue resolution.
  • Troubleshoot and continuously improve system accuracy, speed, robustness, and performance in production environments.
  • Build and maintain operator-facing dashboards and user interfaces to improve visibility, usability, and decision-making.

Data Analysis, Model Optimization & Continuous Improvement

  • Utilize operational and model performance metrics to improve detection accuracy, precision, recall, throughput, and system effectiveness.
  • Establish best practices for computer vision deployment, data management, and model maintenance in industrial environments.
  • Research and evaluate emerging AI, machine vision, robotics, and digital transformation technologies to identify opportunities for innovation.

Technical Leadership, Documentation & Cross-Functional Support

  • Serve as a technical resource for advanced vision, OCR, and AI-driven inspection initiatives.
  • Document system architecture, development methods, testing results, and performance metrics to support scalability and knowledge sharing.
  • Support team success by sharing technical expertise, assisting engineers and staff, and contributing to cross-functional improvement initiatives.

Quality, Safety & Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with company standards, customer requirements, and applicable regulations while promoting safety, quality, and operational excellence.
  • Support continuous improvement activities that strengthen manufacturing quality and process performance.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Strong technical problem-solving and analytical skills
  • Proficiency in Python programming
  • Experience developing software, automation, computer vision, robotics, machine learning solutions or other related STEM activities
  • Knowledge of computer vision and image processing concepts
  • Strong communication, collaboration, and project execution skills
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot and solve complex technical problems

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a manufacturing environment, preferably in automation or advanced manufacturing
  • Strong experience with Computer Vision, AI-based vision solutions, and image processing applications
  • Proficiency in Python programming for automation, data analysis, vision system development, and manufacturing digital transformation projects
  • Experience developing and implementing Manufacturing DX solutions to improve performance, traceability, and decision-making
  • Basic understanding of PLC controls, including Allen-Bradley/Rockwell Automation, tag structures, and ladder logic
  • Familiarity with industrial connectivity tools such as Kepware
  • Experience with software development tools such as Visual Studio Code, Github Copilot, and GitLab
  • Knowledge of Neural Networks and machine learning concepts related to industrial vision applicationsExperience with Apriso integration or similar manufacturing software platforms

Education Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Robotics, Mechatronics, Automation, or a related technical field. Equivalent combinations of education and demonstrated experience in automation, computer vision, software development, or manufacturing technology will be considered.

In lieu of a degree, we consider equivalent, job-related experience, military service, professional certifications, and demonstrated skills. Equivalency determinations are made based on the essential functions of the role.

Language Requirements

Must be able to read, write, understand, and communicate effectively in English.

Work Environment

The physical demands and work environmental characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the team member must have the ability to work in extreme hot or cold conditions, stand for the duration of the shift, uses hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools or controls; reach with hands and arms; ascend stairs; balance; stoop, kneel or crouch; talk and hear. In addition, the team member must occasionally lift up to (“20”, “50”, etc.) lbs. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and the ability to focus.

$42.92/hr

title: Fire Sprinkler Apprentice
description:
The Hiller Companies, LLC has an immediate opening for Fire Sprinkler Apprentice. If you are a dedicated professional with a passion for fire protection and safety, we invite you to apply today.

With over 100 years in the industry, our mission is to ensure the highest standard of safety and innovation in comprehensive fire protection services, including installation, inspection, maintenance and repair of critical fire and life safety equipment. Our team remains laser-focused on one goal - making the world a safer place.

Job Summary: Fire sprinkler apprentices assist senior technicians in the installation and service of fire sprinkler systems, while receiving on the job training.

Pay Range: $17.00/hour - $22.00/hour. The posted salary range reflects the anticipated hiring range for this position at the time of posting and is provided in accordance with applicable pay transparency laws. Actual starting pay will be determined based on job-related factors, including the candidate's qualifications, experience, skills, education, internal equity, geographic location (where applicable), and market considerations. Not all candidates will be hired at the top of the posted range. The posted range reflects base salary only and does not include any applicable bonuses, commissions, overtime, or the value of employee benefits. Eligible employees may participate in the Company's benefit programs, subject to the terms and eligibility requirements of each plan.

Key Responsibilities

Assist in the Inspection, Testing, and Maintenance of Fire Sprinkler Systems:

· Assist senior technicians in performing routine inspections, testing, and maintenance of fire sprinkler systems.

· Handle tools, testing equipment, and materials under supervision.

· Assist with inspecting sprinkler heads, valves, piping, gauges, and other system components for proper condition and operation.

· Support the testing of waterflow switches, tamper switches, main drains, inspector's test connections, and other system components.

· Assist with routine maintenance and minor repairs, including replacing defective components as directed by senior technicians.

Collaborate with the Service and Inspection Team:

· Work closely with senior technicians to ensure inspections, testing, and maintenance activities are completed efficiently and accurately.

· Follow instructions and procedures provided by supervisors and experienced technicians.

· Communicate effectively with team members to coordinate daily assignments and service activities.

· Assist in identifying and documenting deficiencies discovered during inspections and testing.

Prepare for Inspection, Testing, and Maintenance Activities:

· Assist in reviewing inspection reports, service histories, and available system documentation.

· Prepare work areas by ensuring safe and appropriate access to sprinkler system components.

· Gather and organize necessary tools, testing equipment, replacement parts, and materials.

· Assist with completing inspection reports, documenting test results, and recording deficiencies accurately.

Follow Safety Guidelines and Industry Regulations:

· Adhere to company safety policies and wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE).

· Follow applicable NFPA standards, including NFPA 25, and local fire codes and regulations.

· Follow proper procedures when isolating, draining, testing, and restoring fire sprinkler systems under supervision.

· Report safety concerns, system impairments, and hazardous conditions to senior technicians or supervisors.

· Ensure work areas are maintained in a clean, organized, and safe condition.

Learn and Develop Technical Skills:

· Actively participate in training sessions and hands-on learning opportunities related to fire sprinkler inspection, testing, maintenance, and repair.

· Develop familiarity with wet, dry, preaction, and deluge sprinkler systems and their associated components.

· Learn proper inspection and testing procedures in accordance with NFPA 25 and applicable requirements.

· Develop the ability to identify common deficiencies, recognize system impairments, and understand basic troubleshooting procedures.

· Work toward obtaining relevant industry certifications and qualifications as applicable.

· Seek guidance from senior technicians to continuously improve technical knowledge and field capabilities.

description:

The IT Systems Administrator is a hands-on position which will own and operate the tools, endpoints, and infrastructure that keep our people, our network, and our field deployments running securely and reliably. You'll be the dedicated LEXSO-side counterpart to our parent company's IT function, building and administering the systems specific to our environment while coordinating with Constellis IT on shared services.   • Administer user account lifecycle across core systems including onboarding, role changes, and offboarding

QUALIFICATIONS

title: Director, Integrated Media
description:
The Director, Integrated Media leads the planning, buying, and optimization of paid media across search, AI paid advertising, aggregators, direct mail, email, programmatic, paid social, and traditional media channels. Reporting to the Managing Director, Direct Marketing, this leader owns the integrated media strategy that drives profitable customer acquisition for the direct-to-consumer business.

This role manages an in-house media team and partners closely with the Director of Brand Strategy and the Director of Data & Analytics: together they inform every media buy, ensuring that upper-funnel awareness and lower-funnel acquisition investments work as one integrated plan. The ideal candidate combines deep channel expertise with strong analytical judgment and the ability to develop and inspire a high-performing team.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Strategy & planning: Develop and execute an integrated, multi-channel media strategy and annual plan that aligns with growth, retention, and profitability goals.
  • Brand Strategy partnership: Collaborate closely and continuously with the Director of Brand Strategy to align media plans with brand positioning, audience insights, messaging, and creative direction, so that every buy reinforces the brand and supports awareness and consideration goals.
  • Data & Analytics partnership: Partner with the Director of Data & Analytics to inform all media buys with audience analysis, attribution, incrementality testing, forecasting, and performance insights; jointly set KPIs and review results on a regular cadence.
  • Full-funnel investment: Balance investment across upper-funnel awareness and lower-funnel acquisition channels, define success measures for each stage, and shift spend as results warrant.
  • Traditional media: Lead strategy, planning, and investment for all traditional media, including video (linear, streaming, and connected TV), audio (radio, streaming, and podcast), and out of home; oversee negotiation, buying, and measurement with publisher partners.
  • Budget & performance: Own the media budget and allocate spend across channels based on performance and market conditions; manage to efficiency and volume targets.
  • Measurement & optimization: Partner with Data and Analytics to establish attribution, testing, and reporting frameworks; use insights to continually improve efficiency and customer quality.
  • Team leadership: Lead, coach, and develop Media Team; set clear goals, build a culture of accountability and learning, and plan for talent and succession.
  • Vendor & partner management: Manage relationships and negotiations with publishers, vendors, and platforms to secure favorable terms and access to new opportunities.
  • Operational excellence: Oversee marketing operations and trafficking processes to ensure accurate, timely, and scalable campaign execution.
  • Innovation: Stay ahead of changes in media industry and competitive environment; pilot and scale new channels, tools, and capabilities.
  • Executive communication: Report on performance, forecasts, and strategic recommendations to senior leadership.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or a related field; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
  • Experience: 10+ years of experience in performance or direct-response marketing and media buying, including 5+ years leading and developing managers and teams.
  • Channel expertise: Proven success managing large budgets across multiple paid channels, including search, programmatic, paid social, direct mail, email, video, audio and out of home.
  • Full-funnel experience (required): Demonstrated experience developing and managing both upper-funnel awareness channels and lower-funnel acquisition strategy, with a track record of connecting brand investment to acquisition results.
  • Cross-functional partnership: Proven ability to partner with brand strategy and data and analytics leaders to inform media decisions.
  • Analytical skills: Strong command of attribution, testing, and media measurement, with the ability to translate data into actionable decisions.
  • Leadership: Demonstrated ability to build, motivate, and retain high-performing teams in a collaborative environment.
  • Communication: Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders.
  • Preferred: Experience in insurance or other regulated financial services, and familiarity with emerging media platforms.

The pay range for this position is $175,000 to $230,000 annually. Actual compensation will vary based on multiple factors, including employee knowledge and experience, role scope, business needs, geographical location, and internal equity.​

title: Internship - Time Series Foundation Models for Forecasting
description:
ABOUT CFM


Founded in 1991, we are a global quantitative and systematic asset management firm applying a scientific approach to finance to develop alternative investment strategies that create value for our clients.
We value innovation, dedication, collaboration, and the ability to make an impact. Together, we create a stimulating environment for talented and passionate experts in research, technology, and business to explore new ideas and challenge existing assumptions.

Your Role

The Data-Human-Insights team works across a wide variety of structured and unstructured datasets, from time series to graphs, assessing their predictive power and preparing them for modeling. As data scientists, we work closely with the Research team to extract valuable insights from the data.

Accurate and efficient time series forecasting is central to CFM's work, and it sits at one of the most important intersections between the expertise and interests of researchers and data scientists. The literature is large and growing, spanning econometrics, operations research, traditional machine learning, deep learning and generative AI. In recent years, time series foundation models have become a performant and popular option for a wide variety of forecasting tasks.

The goal of this internship is to survey and evaluate existing time series foundation models against CFM's needs, and to identify where they can improve on the forecasting methods we use today. Building on this evaluation, you will research, propose and implement techniques to adapt these models to our purposes, and help plan and develop their integration into different workloads across the firm.

You will be expected to understand, implement, evaluate and operationalize contemporary research on time series foundation models, and to test it as rigorously out of sample as any other model we use

Key Responsibilities

  • Survey the academic and industry literature on time series foundation models and identify the most relevant approaches.
  • Benchmark existing models against current forecasting methods, including classical approaches (ARIMA, GARCH, state space models).
  • Propose and implement techniques to improve these models for CFM's use cases (e.g. fine-tuning with LoRA, quantization, architectural adaptations).
  • Evaluate models rigorously out of sample, avoiding look-ahead bias and data leakage.
  • Aggregate and join heterogeneous data sources and process huge datasets efficiently.
  • Help plan and develop the integration of selected models into different workloads.
  • Write clear documentation and reports on your methodology, results and limitations, and present them to the team and, occasionally, to researchers.

Your Skills

You are in final year of a Master's degree or engineering school program in data science, statistics, applied mathematics, computer science or a related field.

You are proficient in Python, pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch and Matplotlib.

You have experience manipulating and modeling time series, with a solid grounding in classical approaches such as ARIMA, GARCH and state space models.

You have experience with modern deep learning and generative AI architectures and techniques, such as transformers, attention mechanisms, positional encodings, fine-tuning with LoRA, and quantization.

You understand how to evaluate forecasting models out of sample, including how to avoid look-ahead bias and data leakage.

You can aggregate and join heterogeneous data sources and manipulate huge datasets.

You can conduct independent literature reviews, propose new ideas, and synthesize results, challenges and proposals.

You are proactive, with a drive to experiment and propose original ideas.

You communicate results and limitations clearly and concisely.

You are fluent in English.

You are available for a six-month internship.

We believe that our diversity, breadth of experience, and multiple points of view are among the leading factors in our success.

The Director serves as the primary business leader responsible for understanding how Plymouth Rock competes, performs, and grows across agency, partnership, and comparative rater distribution channels.

The position will partner closely with Product Management, Distribution, Marketing, IT, Operations, Underwriting, and Financial Planning to identify opportunities that improve growth, retention, profitability, agency productivity, and customer acquisition effectiveness.

This is a working management position requiring both strong leadership capabilities and the ability to personally conduct analyses, develop recommendations, and influence business decisions.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Comparative Rater Strategy & Optimization

  • Develop and execute Plymouth Rock's comparative rater strategy, including platform optimization, vendor management, implementation governance, and long-term roadmap planning.
  • Serve as the primary relationship owner with comparative rater vendors, driving improvements in quote performance, agent experience, carrier visibility, and operational efficiency.
  • Partner with Product, Underwriting, and IT teams to ensure product, rate, underwriting, and filing changes are accurately implemented across comparative rating platforms.
  • Lead optimization of comparative rater workflows, including eligibility rules, company-specific questions, defaults, quote return performance, carrier visibility logic, and quality assurance processes.
  • Monitor comparative rater performance and develop recommendations to improve agency adoption, quoting efficiency, and policy conversion.

Competitive Intelligence & Market Strategy

  • Lead Plymouth Rock's competitive intelligence efforts within the Partners distribution channel by monitoring pricing position, product competitiveness, quoting performance, market trends, and competitor activity. Collaborate with stakeholders in Product Management and IT to drive improvements in these results.
  • Develop competitive intelligence frameworks, dashboards, and executive reporting that benchmark Plymouth Rock's performance and identify opportunities to improve market share, profitability, and growth.
  • Analyze competitive positioning by state, product, agency segment, and distribution channel and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Monitor comparative rating technology, insurtech innovation, and emerging market trends while supporting Product and Distribution leadership in evaluating opportunities and threats.

Distribution Analytics & Business Performance

  • Deliver performance measurement, business intelligence, and decision support across partnership, agency, and comparative rater distribution channels.
  • Develop executive dashboards, KPI frameworks, and management reporting that measure growth, retention, profitability, agency productivity, customer acquisition effectiveness, and overall distribution performance.
  • Partner with Finance to optimize agency economics, compensation effectiveness, producer productivity, customer lifetime value, and channel profitability to support investment decisions and resource allocation.
  • Partner with Distribution, Product, and Marketing leadership to identify, prioritize, and execute initiatives that increase quote volume, policy growth, partner productivity, and distribution profitability.
  • Support business development efforts through partner evaluations, business case development, growth opportunity analysis, and strategic planning.
  • Ensure reporting accuracy, analytical consistency, data governance, and effective use of data across the organization.

Leadership & Stakeholder Management

  • Lead and develop a high-performing team responsible for comparative rater optimization, competitive intelligence, reporting, analytics, and business performance insights.
  • Establish priorities, allocate resources, and manage team workloads to support strategic business objectives.
  • Build strong partnerships across Product, Distribution, Marketing, Finance, IT, Operations, Underwriting, and Financial Planning teams.
  • Present findings, recommendations, and strategic initiatives to executive leadership and translate complex analytical findings into actionable business decisions.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Actuarial Science, Business Analytics, Computer Science, Finance, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in insurance analytics, competitive intelligence, distribution strategy, product management, pricing, business intelligence, or related disciplines.
  • Minimum 5 years of leadership experience managing analytical, strategic, or business performance teams.
  • Strong knowledge of personal lines insurance, agency distribution models, customer acquisition strategies, and channel economics.
  • Experience with comparative rating platforms such as Vertafore, EZLynx, PL Rating, EPIC, Bolt, or similar technologies preferred.
  • Advanced SQL proficiency and experience working with large-scale data environments.
  • Strong analytical and reporting skills utilizing Excel, Tableau, Power BI, SAS, Python, R, or similar tools.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence product, pricing, underwriting, marketing, and distribution strategies through analytical insights and business recommendations.
  • Exceptional communication, problem-solving, and strategic planning skills.

Key Success Metrics

  • Comparative rater quote volume growth
  • Quote-to-bind conversion performance
  • Share of #1 and Top 3 quote positions
  • Competitive positioning versus key market competitors
  • Independent and captive agency premium growth
  • Agency productivity and retention performance
  • Customer acquisition and conversion effectiveness
  • Distribution profitability and channel economics
  • Reporting accuracy and timeliness
  • Comparative rater implementation quality
  • Adoption and utilization of analytical insights
  • Executive stakeholder satisfaction

SALARY RANGE

The pay range for this position is $186,500 to $247,000 annually. Actual compensation will vary based on multiple factors, including employee knowledge and experience, role scope, business needs, geographical location, and internal equity.​

PERKS & BENEFITS

  • Annual 401(k) Employer Contribution

The Plymouth Rock Company and its affiliated group of companies write and manage over $2 billion in personal and commercial auto and homeowner’s insurance throughout the Northeast and mid-Atlantic, where we have built an unparalleled reputation for service. We continuously invest in technology, our employees thrive in our empowering environment, and our customers are among the most loyal in the industry. title: Controls Technician
description:
Job Summary

We are seeking a driven and results-oriented Controls Technician to support and improve automation systems in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. This role is ideal for a hands-on technical professional who thrives on troubleshooting industrial control systems, optimizing equipment performance, and driving continuous improvement initiatives. As a key partner to Engineering, Maintenance, and Production teams, you will install, maintain, and support PLC-based automation systems, HMIs, industrial networks, and vision systems to enhance operator safety, equipment reliability, product quality, and manufacturing efficiency.

If you enjoy solving complex automation and controls challenges, working with advanced manufacturing technologies, and making a direct impact on operational performance and digital transformation initiatives, this is an excellent opportunity to grow your career in industrial automation and manufacturing excellence.

Benefits

  • 401(k) plan with company match
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Earned paid time off (ETO)
  • 10 paid company holidays annually
  • Performance-based merit increases
  • Annual bonus opportunity

Core Responsibilities

PLC Controls, Programming & System Integration

  • Install, program, troubleshoot, and maintain PLC-based automation systems to support safe, reliable, and efficient manufacturing operations.
  • Develop, modify, and optimize control logic using Allen-Bradley/Rockwell Automation platforms, including ladder logic, tag structures, HMI development, and networked control systems.
  • Support commissioning, startup, and integration of new equipment, automation systems, and production line improvements.
  • Collaborate with engineering and production teams to identify and implement automation solutions that improve productivity, quality, and operational performance.

Electrical Controls & Equipment Reliability

  • Troubleshoot and resolve electrical, controls, and automation issues to minimize downtime and improve equipment reliability.
  • Maintain and support industrial control hardware, including PLCs, HMIs, VFDs, sensors, safety devices, servos, and industrial communication networks.
  • Perform root cause analysis of equipment failures and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
  • Support preventive and predictive maintenance activities for automated manufacturing systems.

Computer Vision & Advanced Automation Support

  • Support the integration and maintenance of computer vision inspection systems within manufacturing processes.
  • Interface vision systems with PLCs, HMIs, and production equipment to enable automated inspection, error-proofing, and process verification.
  • Troubleshoot communication, hardware, and operational issues associated with vision-guided automation systems.
  • Assist in evaluating and deploying emerging automation, vision, sensing, and robotics technologies to improve manufacturing performance.

Continuous Improvement & Process Optimization

  • Develop and implement automation improvements that enhance operator safety, product quality, throughput, and manufacturing efficiency.
  • Lead or support continuous improvement initiatives related to automation, controls, and digital manufacturing technologies.
  • Utilize operational data and production metrics to identify opportunities for process optimization and waste reduction.
  • Support lean manufacturing objectives through automation and controls improvements.

Technical Support, Documentation & Collaboration

  • Serve as a technical resource for controls, automation, and manufacturing system troubleshooting.
  • Create and maintain electrical schematics, control system documentation, program backups, and operating procedures.
  • Train and support maintenance, engineering, and production personnel on automation systems and best practices.
  • Contribute to cross-functional projects and support knowledge sharing across departments.

Quality, Safety & Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with company standards, customer requirements, and applicable safety regulations while promoting a culture of quality and operational excellence.
  • Support quality initiatives through effective controls design, process monitoring, and error-proofing solutions.
  • Maintain adherence to electrical safety standards, machine safety requirements, and plant policies.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Strong technical troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to diagnose and resolve electrical, controls, and automation system issues in a manufacturing environment.
  • Proficiency with PLC programming and troubleshooting.
  • Effective communication and presentation of technical information to engineering, maintenance, and operations teams.
  • Ability to support multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced production environment.
  • Knowledge of manufacturing methods, quality systems, and continuous improvement principles.
  • Understanding of industrial automation systems, electrical controls, and machine integration.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Allen-Bradley/Rockwell Automation platforms.
  • Experience with HMIs, VFDs, servo systems, industrial sensors, and safety control systems.
  • Knowledge of industrial communication networks, including Ethernet/IP and related automation protocols.
  • Experience integrating automated equipment, robotics, vision systems, and manufacturing controls.
  • Familiarity with Computer Vision systems and their integration with PLC-controlled manufacturing processes.
  • Experience with industrial connectivity tools such as Kepware, OPC, or similar communication platforms.
  • Experience supporting Manufacturing DX initiatives, data collection systems, and production monitoring solutions.
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and control panel documentation.
  • Experience with robot programming, commissioning, and system integration.


Education Requirements

High School Diploma or GED.

Language Requirements
Must be able to read, write, understand, and communicate effectively in English.

Work Environment
The physical demands and work environmental characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the team member must have the ability to work in extreme hot or cold conditions, stand for the duration of the shift, uses hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools or controls; reach with hands and arms; ascend stairs; balance; stoop, kneel or crouch; talk and hear. In addition, the team member must occasionally lift up to (“20”, “50”, etc.) lbs. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and the ability to focus.

The information provided in the description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by incumbents within the classification. This description is not intended to be a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, qualifications and working conditions required of employees assigned to this job/classification. This job is intended to include the current essential functions of the job. Management reserves the right to add or modify the duties and responsibilities and to designate other functions as essential at any time.

title: Engineering Summer College Internship
description:
Engineering Intern

Location: Gainesville & Jefferson, Georgia
Company: Kubota Manufacturing of America (KMA)
Duration: 12-Week Internship
Schedule: Full-Time, 40 Hours per Week

Build Your Future with Kubota

Kubota Manufacturing of America (KMA) is one of North America's premier manufacturing operations, producing tractors, turf equipment, utility vehicles, and implements that help customers worldwide succeed in agriculture, construction, and land maintenance. Since opening in Gainesville, Georgia, in 1988 with just 35 employees, KMA has grown into a world-class manufacturing organization spanning more than 3 million square feet across three campuses and employing over 3,000 team members. Our continued growth is driven by innovation, operational excellence, and a commitment to developing future talent.

If you're looking for an opportunity to apply your engineering knowledge in a fast-paced manufacturing environment while making an immediate impact, we'd love to hear from you.

Internship Overview

As an Engineering Intern, you will work alongside experienced engineers and manufacturing professionals to support key initiatives within our production operations. This hands-on opportunity provides exposure to real-world engineering challenges in welding, fabrication, assembly, paint, automation, process improvement, and production support.

Throughout the internship, you'll gain valuable experience applying engineering principles, analyzing manufacturing processes, and contributing to projects that improve safety, quality, productivity, and efficiency.

What You'll Do

Manufacturing Engineering Support
• Support engineering projects within manufacturing, supplier quality, assembly, fabrication, welding, and paint operations.
• Assist engineering teams with process evaluations, implementation activities, and operational improvements.
• Support production operations through data collection, analysis, and troubleshooting activities.

Process Improvement & Analysis
• Assist in the design, development, testing, and implementation of process improvements.
• Analyze production data to identify opportunities to improve efficiency, quality, and cost performance.
• Participate in Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives.
• Support efforts to optimize workflows, reduce waste, and improve operational performance.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Collaborate with Engineering, Production, Quality, Maintenance, and Safety teams to support organizational objectives.
• Participate in team meetings, project reviews, and operational discussions.
• Communicate project progress and recommendations to stakeholders.
Technical Documentation & Reporting
• Create and maintain engineering documentation, reports, work instructions, and technical drawings.
• Assist with preparation of project summaries, presentations, and process documentation.
• Maintain accurate records related to assigned engineering projects and initiatives.
Problem Solving & Production Support
• Participate in troubleshooting equipment, process, and production-related issues.
• Assist engineering personnel in identifying root causes and developing corrective actions.
• Support implementation of solutions that enhance operational effectiveness and reliability.
Innovation & Continuous Improvement
• Contribute innovative ideas that support continuous improvement initiatives throughout the organization.
• Present project findings, recommendations, and results to engineering and leadership teams.
• Participate in intern programs, networking activities, and professional development opportunities.
General Support
• Perform special projects and other related duties as assigned.

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing
    Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.

title: Auto Property Damage Claims Associate (June/July 2027 Start)
description:
Auto Property Damage Claims Associate (June/July 2027 Start)

Position Overview

Plymouth Rock Assurance is seeking motivated, customer-focused candidates graduating in May 2027 to join our Auto Property Damage (Auto PD) Claims Unit, with an anticipated start date of June or July 2027.

The Auto Property Damage Claims Associate is responsible for investigating and managing auto property damage claims, evaluating liability, and working toward fair and timely claim resolutions. This entry-level opportunity is ideal for upcoming college graduates interested in building a career in the insurance industry.

The role requires a high level of customer service, patience, and professionalism in a fast-paced environment with significant phone interaction. Successful candidates will demonstrate strong communication, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, along with the ability to navigate challenging conversations professionally.

Target Start Date: June/July 2027

Target Candidates: Students graduating with a bachelor's degree in May 2027 who are available to begin full-time employment in June or July 2027. Previous claims experience is not required. Comparative negligence claims handling experience is a plus.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities

Policy Analysis

  • Investigate and interpret policy provisions, endorsements, and conditions to determine coverage for automobile property damage claims.
  • Identify and investigate contested coverage claims that may require a roundtable discussion.

Claim Investigation

  • Investigate auto accidents to assess liability by interviewing first- and third-party claimants, witnesses, investigating officers, and other relevant parties.
  • Secure and analyze pertinent records, documentation, and loss scene information to determine proximate cause, negligence, and damages.

Claims Management

  • Evaluate and adjust reserves as necessary.
  • Prepare dispatch instructions for field personnel to inspect vehicles.
  • Negotiate and settle claims within individual authority limits, seeking supervisor approval for claims exceeding authority or requiring additional guidance.
  • Maintain effective follow-up systems on pending files and communicate claim status to insureds, claimants, and brokers.
  • Act as an intermediary between the company, preferred vendors, and customers to resolve disputes.
  • Ensure compliance with privacy guidelines, applicable laws, and claims handling regulations.

Subrogation and Legal Handling

  • Investigate and initiate subrogation processes when applicable.
  • Handle and respond to Special Civil Part lawsuits or intercompany arbitrations related to auto property damage claims.

Administrative Duties

  • Manage a customer-focused phone environment by answering calls, returning voicemails, and responding to emails and text correspondence promptly.
  • Process incoming and outgoing mail in a timely manner and in accordance with state guidelines.
  • Complete other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Education

  • Bachelor's degree required; candidates graduating in May 2027 are encouraged to apply.
  • Previous auto property damage claims experience is welcome but not required.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, organizational, analytical, and customer service skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and general computer applications.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks, manage multiple responsibilities, and work effectively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and a willingness to learn.
  • Ability to handle challenging customer interactions with patience, empathy, and professionalism.

Perks and Benefits:

  • 4 weeks accrued paid time off + 8 paid national holidays per year & 2 floating holidays
  • Free onsite gym at our Boston Location
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • Low cost and excellent coverage health insurance options that start on Day 1 (medical, dental, vision)
  • Robust health and wellness program and fitness reimbursements
  • Auto and home insurance discounts
  • Matching gift opportunities
  • Annual 401(k) Employer Contribution (up to 7.5% of your base salary)
  • Various Paid Family leave options including Paid Parental Leave
  • Resources to promote Professional Development (LinkedIn Learning and licensure assistance
  • Convenient location directly across from South Station and Pre-Tax Commuter Benefits

Salary Range: $50,000 - $55,000 a year. Actual compensation will vary based on multiple factors, including employee knowledge and experience, role scope, business needs, geographical location, and internal equity.

About the Company

The Plymouth Rock Company and its affiliated group of companies write and manage over $2 billion in personal and commercial auto and homeowner’s insurance throughout the Northeast and mid-Atlantic, where we have built an unparalleled reputation for service. We continuously invest in technology, our employees thrive in our empowering environment, and our customers are among the most loyal in the industry. The Plymouth Rock group of companies employs more than 1,900 people and is headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. Plymouth Rock Assurance Corporation holds an A.M. Best rating of “A-/Excellent”.

title: TPO Utility
description:
1. Primary Function:

This individual will need to perform necessary tasks to maintain the proper flow of material at the TPO line, compounding and blending. The responsibilities include operation of extruder, calendar, winder through packaging to produce quality TPO sheeting products and operation of compounding and blending.

  1. Duties and Responsibilities (tasks include but are not limited to):

  • Complete production and quality paperwork.
  • Following TPM program
  • Maintaining 5s
  • Set up equipment and produce product following processing specifications.
  • Assume role of Team Leader when required due to vacations, meetings and absenteeism of TPO Team Leader.
  • Calculate and report output.
  • Identify product and track output using SFIS equipment.
  • Complete maintenance workorders.
  • Verify accuracy of productivity and quality information generated for the shift, pursue required corrections.
  • Train new crewmembers.
  • Complete T3P’s, Non-Standard T3P’s and STP’s.

  • Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • Essential Full Performance Knowledge: Knowledge of the processing specs and grading standards for all the products produced on the TPO line, Compounding and Blending. Knowledge of the operation of the SFIS, NDC and the HMI. Knowledge of the operation of an extruder, 3 roll calender, bridge crane, sheet winder and the packaging of TPO sheeting. Knowledge of safety aspects of all equipment operated as well as the plant’s general safety policies.
  • Essential Full Performance Skills:

  • Reading – Processing specifications, grading standards, EDC prompts, SFIC prompts, gauges, meters, etc.
  • Math – Calculations of output, sheet length, linear feet, and solve basic algebraic equations.
  • Writing – Complete work orders, log book entry, complete incident reports, production and quality paperwork.
  • Communication – instruct crew, train new crew members, complete crew safety training, lead team problem solving groups.
  • Computer skills – SFIS computer, outlook, word, excel necessary for sending electronic communications, writing reports, preparing postings, developing check sheets, and preparing or updating method sheets.
  • Operation of measurement gauges – digital thickness gauge, tape measure and scales.
  • Problem solving skills
  • Leadership skills
  • Forklift operation

  • Essential Full Performance Abilities: N/A

  1. Equipment/Data:

  • Equipment Run On-the-Job: Forklift, overhead cranes, twin screw mixer and auxiliary equipment, 3 roll calender and auxiliary equipment, compounding line and auxiliary equipment, blending and auxiliary equipment, SFIS terminals and printers.
  • Tools Required On-the-Job: Knives, scissors, thickness gauges, tape measure, pencils and miscellaneous hand tools for minor adjustments.
  • Data Used On-the-Job: Processing specifications, grading standards, internal office memos, quality reports, production schedules, SFIS reports and electronic communications.

  1. Education & Experience Requirements:

  • Education: High School Diploma

Equivalency: GED

  1. Work Environment/Time Worked:
    • Work Environment: Activities occur inside a TPO manufacturing facility. Job conditions include but are not limited to exposure to the following.
    • Potential for temperatures exceeding 100 degrees F.
    • Fumes from solvent.
    • Moving mechanical parts including conveyors, turret, core hopper, etc.
    • Pinch points on moving mechanical parts.
    • Heavy equipment operation including forklift and hoist.
    • Heavy equipment includes fork truck.
    • Powders
    • Combustible dust

  • Time Worked:
    1. Days of Week Worked:
      1. Typically Monday through Friday with Saturday and/or Sunday overtime as business dictates.
    2. Shifts Worked:

2-shift rotation (7:00am-3:30pm and 3:00pm-11:30pm) or fixed third shift (11:00pm -7:30am)

  • Physical Requirements:

  1. Climbing steep steps to set-up, inspect and troubleshoot the three levels of a TPO line
  2. Monitor machine performance by watching HMI and NDC screens.
  3. Operate overhead crane
  4. Feel stock to detect off spec situations.
  5. Use fingers to push buttons and turn control settings.
  6. Verbally give instructions in a noisy environment.
  7. Listen to equipment for possible mechanical problems.
  8. Visually inspect material being produced.

Will be required to perform other duties as requested, directed, or assigned.

title: Branch Manager - Military Road
description:
Thank you for your interest in a career at Regions. At Regions, we believe associates deserve more than just a job. We believe in offering performance-driven individuals a place where they can build a career --- a place to expect more opportunities. If you are focused on results, dedicated to quality, strength and integrity, and possess the drive to succeed, then we are your employer of choice.

Regions is dedicated to taking appropriate steps to safeguard and protect private and personally identifiable information you submit. The information that you submit will be collected and reviewed by associates, consultants, and vendors of Regions in order to evaluate your qualifications and experience for job opportunities and will not be used for marketing purposes, sold, or shared outside of Regions unless required by law. Such information will be stored in accordance with regulatory requirements and in conjunction with Regions’ Retention Schedule for a minimum of three years. You may review, modify, or update your information by visiting and logging into the careers section of the system.

Job Description:

At Regions, the Branch Manager is responsible for maintaining an engaged, operationally sound, and high performing team dedicated to improving the financial wellness of our customers. This position acts as a player and coach, oversees branch operations, directly manages associate performance, and provides guidance as needed to ensure associates are helping customers reach their financial goals by understanding and meeting customer needs. Branch Managers are expected to drive branch performance results through strong individual sales performance in addition to ensuring the team meets and exceeds branch sales, quality, and service goals while maintaining an operationally efficient and compliant branch.

Regions' mission is to make life better for our customers and communities, and we are looking for candidates committed to fostering customer relationships, identifying needs and creating a path to achieving financial goals. The successful candidate should be individually driven and competitive, as well as motivated to work as a team to achieve a common goal. This requires a candidate that is motivated by a fast paced and energetic environment, with the ability to provide personalized customer service.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Leads a medium sized team of branch associates responsible for meaningfully impacting new revenue generation through identifying customer needs and providing appropriate guidance and perspective about Regions solutions

  • Conducts outside sales efforts commensurate with market opportunity to generate new business clients while also maintaining and expanding existing consumer and business banking relationships

  • Educates associates, customers, and surrounding community about best practices to achieve and maintain financial wellness in addition to emerging bank technology and digital solutions such as mobile, online and ATM offerings, all designed to make banking easier

  • Coaches and develops branch associates through execution of iConnect - the Region's Sales, Service and Coaching process, with minimal guidance from assigned mentor, senior level managers and internal support partners

  • Provides consistent and timely coaching and guidance to associates to assist with strengthening their product knowledge and identifying customer needs

  • Educates and advises customers on Regions Consumer and Business products and services, including all loan and deposit types in addition to assisting with annuities and life insurance

  • Ensures a consistent optimal customer experience, including handling customer’s transactional needs as needed. This may include sharing responsibility for greeting customers and processing transactions to ensure customers bank when, where, and how they want

  • Resolves escalated customer and associate issues and provides counseling to associates as needed with limited guidance and direction from senior leadership and Human Resources

title: Field CTO, London
description:
Location: London, UK
