ABOUT WEKA

WEKA is architecting a new approach to the enterprise data stack, built for the AI era. The WEKA Data Platform sets the standard for AI infrastructure with a cloud and AI-native software solution that can be deployed anywhere. It transforms legacy data silos into data pipelines that make GPUs, AI, and other performance-intensive workloads run faster, work more efficiently, and consume less energy.

WEKA is a pre-IPO, growth-stage company on a hyper-growth trajectory. We've raised $375M in capital from dozens of world-class venture capital and strategic investors. We help the world's most innovative enterprises and research organizations (including 12 of the Fortune 50), reach discoveries, insights, and outcomes faster and more sustainably.

We're passionate about helping our customers overcome complex data challenges to accelerate their innovation and grow their businesses. If you share our passion, we would love for you to join us on this exciting journey.

WHAT'S COOL ABOUT THIS JOB

As WEKA's Field CTO for EDA and AI, based in London and covering the broader EMEA region, you'll sit at the intersection of two of the most demanding compute domains in the industry: semiconductor design (EDA) and AI infrastructure. You'll work directly with chip designers, foundries, and AI teams across EMEA to architect solutions on the WEKA Data Platform, investigate new innovations across both fields, and champion WEKA as the platform of choice for design and AI workloads. You'll collaborate with the wider CTO Office to translate customer requirements into solutions and architectures, and act as the region's technical evangelist for WEKA in EDA and AI.

RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE

  • Connect WEKA's EDA and AI customers across EMEA to the broader WEKA team, alongside other members of the CTO Office.
  • Partner with the GTM team to develop and deliver compelling technical presentations, demonstrations, and customer workshops that showcase WEKA's value proposition in semiconductor design and AI workloads.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to GTM teams and customers, providing deep technical expertise on how WEKA's technology solves EDA and AI-specific technical and business challenges.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders across product, engineering, and marketing to align customer needs, technology strategy, and product roadmap.
  • Deliver advisory services to the field, working with WEKA's presales and post-sales organizations to drive successful outcomes on both types of engagements.
  • Provide oversight on large, complex EDA and AI customer engagements across the region where appropriate.
  • Champion technical innovation across functions inside and outside GTM, staying current on emerging EDA and AI technologies and assessing their impact on the business.
  • Cultivate partnerships with technology providers (EDA vendors, foundries, hyperscalers, GPU vendors) to address customer requirements and expand WEKA's reach and influence across EMEA.
  • Represent WEKA at industry events, conferences, and workshops across the region, establishing thought leadership in EDA and AI infrastructure.
  • Identify emerging market trends and technologies across EDA and AI to inform product development and go-to-market strategy.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 15+ years of technical experience in relevant industries
  • Proven experience architecting AI infrastructure environments; hands-on experience with EDA (Electronic Design Automation) workflows and semiconductor design compute environments.
  • Proven track record deploying and utilizing multiple AI frameworks and technologies.
  • Excellent English communication and presentation skills, with the ability to engage both technical and non-technical audiences across a diverse regional customer base.
  • Demonstrated experience and proven skills as a technical evangelist, including designing and running customer workshops.
  • Comfortable with frequent travel across EMEA.
  • Ability to translate technical terms into business value for varied audiences, specifically across traditional enterprises adopting AI, foundational model builders, neocloud providers and semiconductor design houses.
  • Experience building and maintaining strong relationships with customers and partners.
  • A collaborative, results-oriented mindset with a strong work ethic and genuine passion for staying ahead of the technology curve.

Concerned you don't meet every qualification? Don't let it stop you from applying.

WEKA is committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. If you're excited about this position but don't meet every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be the right candidate for this or other positions at WEKA.

WEKA is an equal-opportunity employer that prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. We provide equal opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

title: Lead Data Scientist
description:
Plymouth Rock Assurance is on a mission to apply advanced data science to deliver breakthrough insights that propel us to the forefront of personal lines insurance. The Enterprise Data Science team sits at the center of the company, partnering with business leaders to deliver solutions that create durable competitive advantage.

We are seeking a highly motivated and technically skilled lead data scientist to join our collaborative, fast-paced, entrepreneurial team. We are a high-visibility team focused on transformative analytics that drive profitable growth and improve operational performance across the entire enterprise, including Product, Pricing, Underwriting, Claims, Customer Service, and Marketing. This is not a “support” analytics role. You will work on high-impact problems, build production-grade solutions, and use modern machine learning and AI to accelerate discovery, improve decision-making, and reshape how we compete.

Why This Role is Unique

  • Strategic Impact: See the direct business value of your models on core growth and profitability levers across the enterprise.
  • High Visibility: Present directly to the Enterprise Chief Advanced Analytics Officer and other senior executives.
  • End-to-End Ownership: Own solutions from data wrangling and feature engineering through model development, deployment, and monitoring in production.
  • Innovative, Entrepreneurial Environment: Test new ideas quickly in an agile, responsive culture that embraces a “Do It Now” mindset with rigorous measurement and engineering discipline.

Responsibilities:

Depending on level (Data Scientist, Senior, or Lead), you will own projects end-to-end from problem framing through deployment, or lead critical workstreams with broad autonomy:

  • Identify and frame high-value problems across functional areas; translate business questions into analytical strategies, experiments, and measurable outcomes.
  • Develop, test, and deploy predictive models that drive profitable growth and improve operational performance across the enterprise.
  • Apply modern ML and AI techniques to accelerate development cycles, improve model performance, and deliver new capabilities.
  • Build production-ready solutions: robust data pipelines, feature engineering, measurement discipline (KPIs, guardrails, and experiment design), model monitoring, and clear, reproducible documentation aligned to best practices.
  • Communicate with impact: tell the story with data, present recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders, and influence decisions at senior levels.
  • Advance team excellence: evaluate new methods and tools, share reusable components, elevate engineering standards, and (at Senior/Lead) mentor others and help shape technical direction.

Qualifications:

  • PhD in a quantitative field (PhD strongly preferred).
  • Strong foundation in statistics and applied modeling—you can connect theory to practical, business-relevant solutions.
  • Strong hands-on experience with modern modeling tools and methods, including:
    • Python (strongly preferred) and/or R for statistical modeling
    • SQL for large-scale data transformation and analysis
    • GLMs and tree-based methods/GBMs (e.g., H2O, XGBoost, LightGBM); familiarity with clustering, Bayesian methods, regularization, and optimization is a plus
  • Experience with AI (e.g., NLP/LLMs, deep learning, computer vision) applied to feature generation, model development, and business process improvement is helpful but not required.
  • Ability to deliver results in real-world settings: structured problem-solving, experimental mindset, and pragmatic decision-making.
  • Senior candidates must have a proven track record of end-to-end model ownership including shipping models into production, and improving them through monitoring, measurement, and iteration.
  • Strong communication skills—able to present and explain methods, assumptions, tradeoffs, and results clearly.
  • Experience working with cloud and modern data platforms (especially AWS: S3, EC2, SageMaker; and Snowflake).
  • Strong grasp of relational databases and experience working with large, multi-source datasets.
  • Comfort working in Git-based, version-controlled environments; strong documentation practices are required.
  • Insurance industry experience is helpful but not required

Salary Range:

The pay range for this position is $152,000 to $217,000 annually. Actual compensation will vary based on multiple factors, including employee knowledge and experience, role scope, business needs, geographical location, and internal equity.

Perks and Benefits:

  • 4 weeks accrued paid time off + 9 paid national holidays per year
  • Free onsite gym at our Boston Location
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • Low cost and excellent coverage health insurance options that start on Day 1 (medical, dental, vision)
  • Robust health and wellness program and fitness reimbursements
  • Auto and home insurance discounts

  • Annual 401(k) Employer Contribution (up to 7.5% of your base salary)
  • Various Paid Family leave options including Paid Parental Leave

  • Convenient location directly across from South Station and Pre-Tax Commuter Benefits

About the Company

The Plymouth Rock Company and its affiliated group of companies write and manage over $2 billion in personal and commercial auto and homeowner’s insurance throughout the Northeast and mid-Atlantic, where we have built an unparalleled reputation for service. We continuously invest in technology, our employees thrive in our empowering environment, and our customers are among the most loyal in the industry. WEKA is architecting a new approach to the enterprise data stack, built for the AI era. It transforms legacy data silos into data pipelines that make GPUs, AI, and other performance-intensive workloads run faster, work more efficiently, and consume less energy.

We're passionate about helping our customers overcome complex data challenges to accelerate their innovation and grow their businesses. If you share our passion, we would love for you to join us on this exciting journey.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As WEKA's Field CTO for AI Infrastructure in the Americas, based in the San Francisco Bay Area, you will engage with the organizations building and operating the largest GPU environments in the world: neoclouds and NVIDIA Cloud Partners (NCPs), GPU-as-a-service providers, frontier model builders, hyperscalers, and AI-native enterprises moving training and inference into production. This role is distinct from senior sales engineering. You will operate as a peer to customer CTOs and principal engineers, bring an informed perspective on the direction of GPU infrastructure, and carry the internal standing to influence product and engineering priorities when market requirements and the roadmap diverge. Deep expertise in an adjacent domain such as EDA, life sciences, media and entertainment, or financial services is valued, with AI workflows and the infrastructure that supports them as the primary focus. You will collaborate with the broader CTO Office, serve as the region's technical evangelist for WEKA in AI infrastructure, and report directly to WEKA's Head of Solutions Engineering.

RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE

  • Connect WEKA's neocloud, NCP, and AI infrastructure customers across the Americas to the broader WEKA team, alongside other members of the CTO Office.
  • Partner with the GTM team to develop and deliver compelling technical presentations, demonstrations, and customer workshops that showcase WEKA's value proposition for AI training, inference, and multi-tenant GPU cloud workloads.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to GTM teams and customers, providing deep technical expertise on how WEKA solves the architectural and economic challenges of operating GPU infrastructure at scale: multi-tenancy, GPU utilization, inference and token economics, and the data and memory layer beneath AI.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders across product, engineering, and marketing to align customer needs, technology strategy, and product roadmap, and advocate for the field when they are out of sync.
  • Deliver advisory services to the field, working with WEKA's presales and post-sales organizations to drive successful outcomes.
  • Provide oversight on large, complex neocloud and AI customer engagements across the region where appropriate.
  • Champion technical innovation across functions inside and outside GTM, staying current on emerging GPU, networking, inference-serving, and agentic AI technologies and assessing their impact on the business.
  • Cultivate partnerships with technology providers (NVIDIA and the NCP ecosystem, GPU and accelerator vendors, hyperscalers, server and networking partners, orchestration and inference-serving vendors) to address customer requirements and expand WEKA's reach and influence across the Americas.
  • Represent WEKA at industry events, conferences, and workshops across the region, establishing thought leadership in AI infrastructure, neocloud architecture, and inference economics.
  • Identify emerging market trends and technologies across AI infrastructure to inform product development and go-to-market strategy.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 15+ years of technical experience in relevant industries.
  • Proven experience architecting large-scale AI infrastructure environments, including GPU compute, high-performance storage, and the networking and data pipelines around them.
  • Hands-on experience in a senior technical role inside a neocloud, NVIDIA Cloud Partner, GPU-as-a-service provider, or hyperscaler AI platform, with credibility among the people who build and run those environments.
  • Deep understanding of multi-tenant GPU cloud architecture: tenant isolation, scheduling and orchestration (Kubernetes, Slurm), high-performance networking (InfiniBand, RoCE), and the data layer that determines GPU utilization.
  • Proven track record deploying and utilizing multiple AI frameworks and technologies across training and inference.
  • Domain expertise in an adjacent vertical such as EDA, life sciences, media and entertainment, or financial services is preferred; AI workflows and infrastructure remain the primary focus.
  • Demonstrated experience and proven skills as a technical evangelist, including public speaking, published technical content, and designing and running customer workshops.
  • Ability to translate technical terms into business value for varied audiences, specifically across neocloud and AI cloud providers, foundational model builders, hyperscalers, and traditional enterprises adopting AI.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to hold credibility with a principal engineer and a CIO in the same day.

title: Senior Data Governance Analyst
description:
Plymouth Rock is transitioning to an AI/ML-driven operating model. The Data Management team within the Data Office will build and deploy an enterprise data governance framework. This framework will ensure data is trusted, secure, compliant, and accessible through Business Intelligence, Machine Learning (ML), and Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications. The team will promote a culture where data is treated as a strategic asset and company resource, with clear accountability for its quality, use and capture.

You will work closely with other Data Office members, IT groups, AI/ML teams, and business partners to drive adoption of enterprise data policies and standards, improve data quality, and reduce data loss/duplication and technical debt on the data platform.

Responsibilities:

  • Support the Data Management leader to design and implement a comprehensive data governance operation aligned to Plymouth Rock’s AI/ML-first data strategy, which includes:
    • Informing, influencing, and obtaining buy-in from the entire company on the importance of data governance on business objectives and AI/ML imperative.
    • Developing policies, standards, metrics, tools, and processes to ensure robust and comprehensive documentation of data inventories, meaning, permissions, lineage and quality for downstream enterprise development and application.
    • Driving engagement and adoption with data owners, producers, stewards, AI/ML teams, and stakeholders (such as Legal, Audit/Risk, and Information Security)
  • First Priority for the team and you is:
    • Assess usability and completeness of internal catalogs for data on the platform and other sources. Work with relevant business/IT partners to make data governance updates within the catalog and ensure proper ownership, certification, and lifecycle alignment with enterprise standards.
    • Develop and implement metadata and catalog governance standards, including defining tagging frameworks, creating metadata templates, normalizing existing metadata, and establishing validation processes to ensure consistency and quality across reports, dashboards, and other analytics assets.
  • Define and enforce promotion and lifecycle governance standards, including establishing processes for assets moving through POC, Development, and Production, implementing governance checkpoints, and documenting approval and ownership requirements aligned to data platform modernization goals.
  • Develop and deliver training, enablement, and communication materials to support catalog usage, metadata understanding, and governance adoption, including end-user guidance and stakeholder presentations to promote a data-driven culture.
  • Support the Data Management leader to test and integrate a governance tool for the data platform that would complement the governance operating model.
  • Help design and support responsible AI usage and controls around data privacy, bias, and regulatory compliance, including working with Advanced Analytics and AI teams to follow/implement them in their use cases.
  • Establish and enforce lineage tracking to enable traceability from source systems through downstream consumption.
  • Work with IT and business partners to investigate and address data leakage between insurance operations and data stores.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Data Office, Analytics, and IT teams to ensure consistent adoption of governance practices and support broader enterprise data initiatives.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related field is preferred.
  • SQL proficiency
  • 5+ years of experience in data governance or enterprise data management, including implementing governance frameworks in complex, multi-system environments.
  • Experience supporting AI/ML data requirements, including structured, unstructured, and streaming data.
  • Knowledge of MLOps practices, model versioning and deployment pipelines, and AWS services such as Glue, S3, SageMaker, and Snowflake.
  • Python programming
  • Strong understanding of data privacy, regulatory requirements, and responsible AI practices.
  • Demonstrated ability to successfully work in cross-functional environments with business, technology, and analytics teams.
  • P&C Insurance experience and working familiarity of insurance underwriting operations and platform systems preferred.

The pay range for this position is $105,000 to $140,000 annually. Actual compensation will vary based on multiple factors, including employee knowledge and experience, role scope, business needs, geographical location, and internal equity.

Perks and Benefits:

  • 4 weeks accrued paid time off + 10 paid national holidays per year

  • Various Paid Family leave options including Paid Parental Leave
  • Resources to promote Professional Development (LinkedIn Learning and licensure assistance)
  • Convenient location directly across from South Station and Pre-Tax Commuter Benefits

The Plymouth Rock Company and its affiliated group of companies write and manage over $2 billion in personal and commercial auto and homeowner’s insurance throughout the Northeast and mid-Atlantic, where we have built an unparalleled reputation for service. Title: Software Development Process - Engineer

Job Description:

Our company is seeking a high-caliber Software Development Process Engineer to assist driving software process engineering and quality governance support across our global Controls Software teams. In this role, you will work to standardize, deploy, and continuously improve engineering frameworks across the organization to ensure world-class product quality.

Your mission is to act as a catalyst for organizational change by institutionalizing development best practices, leveraging deep root-cause analysis, and managing data-driven quality systems at scale. You will support defined software quality assurance parameters that are executed, with success measured by the visible first-time yield analysis of the released products.

Key Responsibilities

  • Process Governance & QMS: Oversee the tailored documentation and maintenance of the Documents Inventory List within a large, matrixed Quality Management System (QMS).
  • Metrics & Analytics: Define, deploy, and track software metrics, converting complex performance data into actionable Software Quality Governance Reports.
  • Continuous Improvement: Support cross-functional optimization projects of varying size and complexity, keeping a systematic track of progress in the continuous process improvement project report.
  • Root Cause Analysis (RCA): work on risk assessments and process gap analyses utilizing professional quality control tools (e.g., 5-Why, Fishbone diagrams).
  • Training & Coaching: Instruct diverse software teams to ensure comprehensive process adherence, while standardizing official training records.
  • Operational Leadership: Assist cultural and technical alignment across multiple development methodologies (including Waterfall, Iterative, and Agile) to balance delivery priorities and protect project timelines.

Required Qualifications

  • Education: Educational background in Engineering, Software Development, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline.
  • Experience Baseline: 2-3 years of overall experience working within Software Development or Software Quality Assurance environments.
  • Governance Specialization: At least 1+ year of dedicated experience focused strictly on Software Quality Assurance, software process auditing, or quality governance.
  • Methodology Expertise: Hands-on experience navigating and implementing diverse development frameworks (Waterfall, Iterative, Agile/Scrum, etc.).
  • Organizational Change: A proven track record of deploying industry-leading development techniques and driving process adoption across varying team cultures and complex environments.
  • Quality & Planning Tools: Practical experience using traditional QC problem-solving toolsets along with strong day-to-day proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Visio for mapping and data organization.
  • Leadership & Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills combined with a natural aptitude for leading, educating, and coaching technical teams.
  • Execution Mindset: Strong ability to balance multiple high-velocity priorities with a clear passion for delivering zero-defect products on schedule.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Matrix Environment: Experience managing engineering process workflows in large-scale, matrixed enterprise settings.
  • In-House Tooling: Desirable background or familiarity with building in-house automation, monitoring tools, or automated metrics dashboards using PowerApps, Power BI, or Python.

Core Deliverables Expected in Role

  • Documents Inventory Lists: Complete, compliant, and up-to-date process standard inventories.
  • Quality Governance Reports: Regular, data-driven insights mapping software parameters to performance.
  • Process Gap Analysis Reports: Formally documented process deployment gaps matched with systemic root-cause corrections.
  • Training Log Records: Verifiable proof of execution and adherence regarding organizational software process updates.
  • Process Improvement Project Reports: Active, audited logs showcasing ongoing engineering efficiency and yield enhancements.

Benefits:

Phoenix Technical Solutions offers an attractive compensation and benefits package; including health, dental, vision, STD, LTD, Life, IRA with generous company match, paid holidays, vacation and more. Our global commitment to technological advancement offers opportunities for personal growth and development in a stable, supportive work environment.

This is a full-time role with an expected minimum of working 30+ hours per week.

▪ Design and deliver comprehensive fitness programs based on clients' goals that include appropriate exercise selections, programs that include varied fitness offerings, general nutrition guidelines and teaching a fitness lifestyle.

▪ Demonstrate safe and proper exercise techniques to clients.

▪ Meet minimum productivity expectations servicing clients and group sessions.
▪ Create, maintain, and regularly update progress for each personal training client, following company guidelines.
▪ Assist in member service activities such as fitness seminars, training days, and deliver a positive fitness experience to members and guests through custom coaching sessions.

▪ 2-5 years of experience as a Personal Trainer or Fitness Coach.

title: CUAS Technical Expert
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The C-UAS Technical Expert Position supports the planning, integration, execution, and evaluation of counter-unmanned aircraft system activities for customers throughout the United States and in overseas operating environments. Assignments may support U.S. and allied government organizations, military units, federal agencies, state and local law enforcement, critical-infrastructure operators, defense contractors, technology manufacturers, and other authorized private or commercial entities.

The position provides operational and technical expertise during C-UAS training, system integration, testing and evaluation, technology demonstrations, exercises, site assessments, capability development, and range operations. Candidates can be considered for C-UAS Trainer, C-UAS Integrator and Spectrum Manager roles if eligible based on prior experience.

Personnel may support customer requirements at the Constellis Training Center or deploy to other CONUS and OCONUS locations based on program and mission needs.

Individuals assigned to these positions must possess a strong working knowledge of C-UAS systems, layered-defense principles, tactical operations, threat capabilities, system employment, and the integration of multiple sensors and defeat mechanisms. This includes an understanding of radar, RF detection, electronic warfare, EO/IR, command-and-control, communications, UAS technologies, and authorized kinetic and non-kinetic defeat capabilities.

The C-UAS Technical Expert works directly with customers, operators, instructors, engineers, vendors, range personnel, and program leadership to translate operational requirements into effective training, integration, testing, and employment solutions. Responsibilities may include advising customers on system capabilities and limitations, evaluating system performance, supporting tactical scenario development, identifying integration or coverage deficiencies, and recommending improvements to layered-defense procedures.

Depending on qualifications and assignment requirements, employees may serve as C-UAS instructors, system integrators, spectrum managers, evaluators, technical advisors, or exercise-support personnel. All activities will be performed in accordance with applicable laws, authorities, customer requirements, safety standards, security procedures, range regulations, and company policies.

These are casual, part-time positions supporting intermittent customer and program requirements. Assignments are scheduled based on mission needs, employee availability, technical qualifications, and customer requirements. Work may involve irregular schedules, field conditions, domestic or international travel, and short-duration assignments. No minimum number of work hours is guaranteed.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Serve as a technical and operational C-UAS subject matter expert during training, testing and evaluation, technology demonstrations, exercises, site assessments, and customer engagements.
  • Apply the detect, track, identify, decide, and defeat methodology when planning, evaluating, and supporting layered C-UAS operations.
  • Support the employment and integration of radar, passive RF, electronic warfare, EO/IR, acoustic, command-and-control, communications, kinetic defeat, and non-kinetic defeat capabilities.
  • Evaluate C-UAS system performance, operational suitability, capabilities, limitations, coverage, interoperability, and effectiveness against representative UAS threats.
  • Support layered-defense planning based on the threat, terrain, airspace, electromagnetic environment, mission requirements, protected assets, and available authorities.
  • Advise customers and operational personnel on C-UAS system employment, sensor placement, coverage considerations, engagement procedures, and tactical integration.
  • Operate, configure, inspect, test, and troubleshoot assigned C-UAS systems and associated equipment within individual qualifications and authorization.
  • Support tactical scenarios involving UAS detection, tracking, identification, classification, decision-making, reporting, and authorized defeat procedures.
  • Support C-UAS battle drills, crew drills, command-and-control processes, reporting procedures, and coordination between sensors, operators, decision-makers, and defeat capabilities.
  • Assist with the development, validation, and refinement of C-UAS concepts of operation, SOPs, tactics, techniques, procedures, training materials, test plans, and evaluation criteria.
  • Support realistic threat replication and Red Force activities using representative UAS platforms, flight profiles, tactics, payloads, and operational scenarios.
  • Provide technical observations, operational analysis, after-action feedback, and recommendations following training, testing, demonstrations, and exercises.
  • Maintain accurate system records, test data, training documentation, equipment accountability, configuration information, and operational reports.
  • Coordinate with customers, instructors, range control, safety personnel, UAS operators, vendors, engineers, spectrum personnel, and other Constellis staff.
  • Ensure activities comply with applicable FAA, FCC, DoD, customer, range, airspace, spectrum, safety, security, and information-protection requirements.
  • Maintain technical proficiency on assigned systems, emerging UAS threats, evolving C-UAS technologies, and current operational practices.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • At least three years of relevant C-UAS, air defense, electronic warfare, radar, RF, communications, UAS, military, law enforcement, or technical experience.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of layered C-UAS defense and the integration of multiple detection, tracking, identification, command-and-control, and defeat capabilities.
  • Working knowledge of C-UAS technologies, including radar, RF detection, electronic warfare, EO/IR, C2, communications, kinetic defeat, and non-kinetic defeat systems.
  • Understanding of UAS platforms, threat categories, flight characteristics, mission profiles, payloads, control methods, navigation systems, and common employment tactics.
  • Experience supporting C-UAS operations, training, testing and evaluation, exercises, demonstrations, capability assessments, or system integration.
  • Ability to interpret system manuals, architecture diagrams, SOPs, CONOPS, TTPs, test plans, operational orders, and customer requirements.
  • Ability to identify and clearly communicate system capabilities, limitations, performance deficiencies, integration risks, and operational considerations.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work effectively with military, government, law enforcement, commercial, technical, and executive audiences.
  • Ability to work in classroom, field, range, and austere environments; maintain a flexible schedule; travel periodically; and satisfy applicable background and facility-access requirements.
  • Preferred:
    • Five or more years of C-UAS, air defense, electronic warfare, UAS, or related operational experience.
    • Prior experience supporting DoD, federal, law enforcement, critical-infrastructure, or international customers.
    • Experience with multiple C-UAS platforms or system-of-systems architectures.
    • Experience developing C-UAS doctrine, CONOPS, SOPs, TTPs, training programs, test plans, or capability assessments.
    • Operational experience in deployed, high-threat, or joint and multinational environments.
    • Current or previously held U.S. Government security clearance.

title: Data Science Intern
description:

title: VP, Financial Planning & Analysis
description:
Company Overview:

Lightspeed is the leading provider of cloud-based software for dealerships, serving the Powersport, Marine, RV, Trailer, and Golf Car industries adding hundreds of dealerships to the Lightspeed community each year.
Lightspeed’s Dealer Management Solution (DMS) enables dealerships to optimize their end-to-end business operations, including Sales, Parts, Service, Rentals, Payments, Accounting, and Customer Relationship Management (CRM). When implemented into their daily operations, Lightspeed helps dealers increase their profitability by selling more units, service, and parts, all while creating a more streamlined experience for customers.
Lightspeed is the most complete and integrated DMS in the industry with over 500 integrations with Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), aftermarket parts and accessory distributors and dozens of other software tools that a dealership may use to run their business. Uniquely designed by dealers for dealers, and refined over the past 4 decades, Lightspeed empowers over 4,500+ dealers across North America with the tools and technology they need to manage their dealerships.

Position Summary

The Vice President of FP&A will be a strategic partner to the CFO, key contributor to the finance and accounting organization, and a critical member of the leadership team driving the growth, profitability and success of Lightspeed DMS. This individual will be responsible for delivering financial and operational insights, leading change-management initiatives, and preparing the company for an exit, as well as supporting the ongoing activities of budgeting, forecasting, reporting, business intelligence and managing a team of four analysts.

What You'll Do

Strategic Partnership & Insight

• Be the thought partner to the CFO and Senior Leadership Team on growth, margin, pricing, capital allocation, and M&A.

• Support long-range planning, portfolio analysis, business development, and financing activities through analysis and scenario modeling.

• Turn data into decisions: explain what is driving results, what could change them, and what to do next.

• Link results to strategy: develop analytics and key messages around business performance and connect financial results to business strategies.

• Challenge constructively. Pressure-test assumptions and business cases and hold leaders accountable to their plans.

• Partner with Sales, Customer Success, Product, and Operations so every function understands its financial metrics and value-creation levers.

Planning, Forecasting & Performance Management

• Lead financial planning processes, including budgeting and forecasting with a disciplined cadence and clear accountability.

• Develop financial analysis, modeling, forecasting, and reporting frameworks to ensure efficient financial operations and organizational alignment.

• Lead and manage the capital planning and budget process to ensure alignment with corporate strategy and business goals.

• Build the operating rhythm: monthly business reviews, variance narratives, and KPI scorecards.

• Lead scenario planning to prepare the company for upside, downside, and sponsor-driven value creation targets.

• Sharpen the recurring revenue story: ARR, retention, bookings-to-revenue, unit economics, and cash conversion.

Sponsor, Board & Executive Reporting

• Prepare Board and sponsor materials that are accurate, concise, and tell a consistent story.

• Continuously monitor and improve financial reporting processes, forecasting techniques, and data analysis methods to drive financial insights.

• Review financial statements, reports, and models to develop high-level business insights, create financial projections, and advise on cost management and investment decisions.

• Collaborate with equity sponsors and the Board of Directors as a trusted partner on performance, forecasts, and value creation initiatives.

• Support M&A, financing, and exit activity, including integration planning, synergy tracking, and readiness for a sale of the company.

• Lead change-management initiatives that improve how the company plans, reports, and makes decisions.

Team Leadership & Development

• Provide leadership and vision for the FP&A and business teams, including managing a team of four analysts.

• Lead, coach, and grow the FP&A team, setting clear expectations, giving regular feedback, and building bench strength.

• Lead a team of financial professionals and collaborate with a broad range of stakeholders throughout the company.

• Delegate with trust and accountability, developing people through stretch work.

• Create a culture of ownership, curiosity, and candor where analysts challenge assumptions and raise issues early.

Process, Systems & AI-Enabled Finance

• Modernize how FP&A works: reduce manual effort, shorten cycle times, and shift team time from reporting to insight.

• Identify and pilot AI and automation use cases in forecasting, variance analysis, and reporting, with sound governance and human review.

• Ensure optimal maintenance and ongoing evolution of relevant technology, working closely with Accounting, IT, and Revenue Operations to keep financials aligned with financial applications.

• Be a credible voice on the data foundation: definitions, source of truth, and metric consistency.

What You Should Have

Qualifications

• 8+ years of progressive finance experience in FP&A, strategic finance, or business partnering, with 3+ years leading teams, preferably in a private equity-owned SaaS portfolio company.

• Proven people leader: has hired, developed, and retained strong finance talent, with the ability to lead teams of finance professionals that collaborate with global stakeholders.

• Executive presence and influence: comfortable challenging senior leaders and delivering a clear message to the CFO, CEO, and Board.

• Strong communicator: written and verbal, with the ability to make complex financial topics simple.

• Sound business judgment: prioritizes what matters, frames trade-offs, and recommends a path.

• Thrives in a fast-moving, remote, cross-functional environment with competing priorities.

• Mastery of planning tools: Excel, PowerPoint, Power BI, Claude, etc.

• AI thought partner: experience applying AI and automation to finance workflows.

description:

Overseeing one to three factories and guiding a team of production leaders responsible for hundreds of employees, you will play a critical role in delivering operational excellence. Success in this position requires strong leadership, sound decision-making, and a relentless focus on safety, quality, productivity, and continuous improvement. You will ensure the right resources, priorities, and processes are in place to consistently meet production goals while building a high-performing and engaged workforce.

We have positions in Gainesville, GA and Jefferson, GA

Roles & Responsibilities:

Production Leadership & Operational Execution

  • Owns daily, weekly, and monthly production execution across 1–3 factories, ensuring achievement of output, safety, quality, and cost targets
  • Directly leads and develops Production Managers, ensuring consistent application of standards, priorities, and leadership practices across all shifts
  • Aligns labor, equipment, and materials to rapidly adjust to changing production demand

Safety, Quality & Compliance Assurance

  • Ensures daily compliance with all safety, quality, and environmental standards, actively validating conditions on the factory floor
  • Reinforces PPE usage, standard work, and risk mitigation practices across weld, paint, and assembly environments
  • Partners with plant and quality leadership to address systemic issues and prevent recurrence

Performance Management & Continuous Improvement

  • Monitors and drives performance using KPIs related to throughput, labor efficiency, scrap, downtime, and delivery
  • Leads Kaizen, Lean, and 5-Gen manufacturing initiatives, translating continuous improvement principles into measurable results
  • Identifies bottlenecks and variability, deploying countermeasures rapidly in a fast-paced production environment

Workforce & Talent Management

  • Manages staffing levels and performance across multiple shifts, always ensuring operational coverage and leadership presence
  • Coaches and develops leaders to build accountability, engagement, and bench strength
  • Works closely with HR on employee relations, performance actions, and succession planning

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partners daily with engineering, maintenance, supply chain, logistics, and HR to ensure seamless production flow
  • Balances production priorities with maintenance needs, material availability, and engineering changes
  • Serves as a key operational voice within the manufacturing leadership team

Financial & Resource Accountability

  • Prepares and manages budgets for assigned production areas, controlling labor and operational costs
  • Ensures efficient use of resources while maintaining safety, quality, and delivery standards
  • Supports capital planning and resource justification as needed

Minimum Qualifications (Knowledge, Skills & Abilities):

  • Proven experience (10+ years) in manufacturing operations
  • 5+ years in management or a multi-site leadership role.
  • Experience in management of 300+ employees.
  • Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, quality control, and safety regulations.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive cultural and operational improvements in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent problem-solving and decision-making skills.
  • Exceptional leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills with a demonstrated ability to lead diverse teams.
  • Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or kaizen and driving improvements
  • Ability to prioritize, manage, and execute multiple complex issues occurring simultaneously.
  • Proficiency in manufacturing software and Microsoft Office Suite.

Education Requirements:

Bachelor’s, Associates, or technical degree in engineering, Manufacturing, or a related industry field

In lieu of a degree, we consider equivalent, job-related experience, military service, professional certifications, and demonstrated skills. Equivalency determinations are made based on the essential functions of the role.

Work Environment:

The physical demands and work environmental characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. Ability to work in extreme heat and cold. Ability to work in a loud environment.

Physical Demands:

80% factory, 20% office. While performing the duties of this job, the team member must have the ability to work in the manufacturing environments, in all climates. Hot and cold conditions inside the plants are relative to seasonal changes. Hot/warm conditions for paint shop areas and weld shop areas. Loud noise, weld flash, heavy parts and equipment requires the ability to dawn PPE in all production areas. Large areas of responsibility that require extensive walking and standing. Capable of standing, extensive walking, climbing stairs on a frequent basis without physical constraints. Member must also be able to work extended and flexible work hours to interface with workers on all shifts as well as international business units. Must be physically able to travel domestically and internationally.

title: Electronic Systems Seller
description:

title: Senior Bodily Injury Specialist

Leadership & Analytical Skills – Strong self-motivation, coverage analysis, investigation, and negotiation abilities.

About the Company

The Plymouth Rock Company and its affiliated group of companies write and manage over $2 billion in personal and commercial auto and homeowner’s insurance throughout the Northeast and mid-Atlantic, where we have built an unparalleled reputation for service. We continuously invest in technology, our employees thrive in our empowering environment, and our customers are among the most loyal in the industry. The Plymouth Rock group of companies employs more than 1,900 people and is headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. Plymouth Rock Assurance Corporation holds an A.M. Best rating of “A-/Excellent”.

title: Class 3 Wastewater Apprentice (GV200) (1st Shift)
description:
Are you ready to kickstart your career in the essential field of wastewater treatment? This 1-2 year apprenticeship program is your gateway to obtaining a GA Industrial or Class 3 Wastewater Treatment (WWT) license! Whether you’re starting from scratch or already hold a wastewater license from another state, this program is designed to equip you with the skills and knowledge needed to excel in this vital industry.

What You’ll Learn

During your apprenticeship, you will gain hands-on experience in safely monitoring and maintaining wastewater treatment systems. You’ll dive into a variety of tasks, including performing laboratory and field tests to ensure safe working conditions and top-quality output. You’ll also develop your communication skills, learning how to effectively collaborate with coworkers, supervisors, and other departments.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • System Monitoring: Keep a close eye on the WWT system, ensuring everything runs smoothly.
  • Quality Testing: Conduct various laboratory and field tests to guarantee quality results.
  • Chemical Management: Monitor, calculate, and adjust chemical dosages to optimize the WWT system.
  • Waste Management: Assist with the loading and off-loading of both hazardous and non-hazardous waste, ensuring proper documentation.
  • Equipment Maintenance: Utilize power washers and tools to maintain cleanliness of WWT equipment and perform basic preventative maintenance.
  • Troubleshooting: Identify and resolve issues with pumps, tools, chemical streams, and other equipment to prevent safety, environmental, quality, or productivity problems.
  • Spill Response: Join the spill response team and respond promptly to major spills.
  • Risk Assessments: Conduct periodic safety and quality risk assessments, leading or assisting with corrective actions to lower risks.
  • Workstation Organization: Maintain a 5S compliant workstation to promote efficiency and safety.
  • Communication Protocol: Practice the “Stop, Call, Wait” method to alert appropriate personnel in case of equipment troubles or abnormalities.
  • Compliance Support: Support ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 requirements.
  • Special Projects: Engage in special projects and related tasks as requested.

Essential Skills and Experience

  • License Qualification: Ability to meet the qualifications for a GA WWT Operator License (Industrial/Class 3 or greater).
  • Communication Skills: Strong English language competency and legible writing ability.
  • Math and Chemistry Basics: Basic math and chemistry skills are essential.
  • Tech Proficiency: Familiarity with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Self-Starter: Demonstrated initiative and ability to work independently.
  • Certifications: Must obtain Kubota LOTO and Confined Space Entry certification within 30 days, and Kubota sit-down forklift certification within the same timeframe. You’ll also need to successfully complete a physical fitness test (PFT) within 30 days.
  • HAZWOPER and DOT Certification: Ability to obtain these certifications within 6 months.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Confined Space Experience: Previous experience working in confined spaces is a plus.
  • Laboratory Testing: Familiarity with conducting laboratory tests (such as titrations and metal concentrations).
  • Manufacturing Background: Experience in a manufacturing environment is beneficial.

Working Conditions

This position requires meeting specific physical demands and working conditions that are essential for success. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

Physical Requirements

As part of your role, you may need to:

  • Work in extreme hot or cold conditions.
  • Stand for the duration of your shift and engage in various physical activities, including using your hands for handling tools and controls.
  • Reach, ascend stairs, balance, stoop, kneel, or crouch as necessary.
  • Communicate effectively and maintain awareness through talking and listening.
  • Occasionally lift items weighing up to 50 lbs.
  • Demonstrate various vision abilities, including close and distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to focus.
  • Successfully complete a PFT and respirator fit test.

Direct Reports

There are no direct reports in this position, allowing you to focus on your training and development.

Embark on a rewarding journey in wastewater treatment and make a positive impact on your community! Apply today and take the first step toward a fulfilling career!

Job Summary: A Fire Sprinkler Service Technician is responsible for inspecting, testing, repairing, and maintaining fire sprinkler systems to ensure compliance with regulatory standards and optimal safety for occupants, with an emphasis on repairs and maintenance. You will work closely with clients, contractors, and regulatory authorities to address any issues and maintain the integrity of fire protection systems.

Pay Range: $30- $38 / Hourly. The posted salary range reflects the anticipated hiring range for this position at the time of posting and is provided in accordance with applicable pay transparency laws. Actual starting pay will be determined based on job-related factors, including the candidate's qualifications, experience, skills, education, internal equity, geographic location (where applicable), and market considerations. Not all candidates will be hired at the top of the posted range. The posted range reflects base salary only and does not include any applicable bonuses, commissions, overtime, or the value of employee benefits. Eligible employees may participate in the Company's benefit programs, subject to the terms and eligibility requirements of each plan.

Sign-On Bonus: Qualified technicians will receive a $5,000.00 sign-on bonus paid in two installments: the first payment after successfully completing 30 days of employment, and the second payment after completing 90 days. This bonus rewards your commitment and excellent performance during your initial months with our company.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Conduct routine inspections and testing of wet, dry and pre-action systems fire sprinkler systems, to identify and address any issues or deficiencies, as per NFPA 25 requirements
  • Prepare detailed reports documenting inspection findings, test results, and any related deficiencies or non-compliance issues observed, in accordance with NFPA codes and standards.
  • Test and evaluate system functionality of sprinkler heads, valves, piping, pumps, and control systems.
  • Inspect piping, fittings, and connections for signs of corrosion, leaks, or damage, recommending necessary repairs or replacements
  • Perform maintenance tasks on fire sprinkler systems, such as replacing damaged or malfunctioning components, cleaning pipes and sprinkler heads, lubricating moving parts, and adjusting system settings to ensure optimal performance
  • Inspect Fire pump assemblies, including testing flow rates, pressure levels, and mechanical integrity
  • Respond promptly to service calls and emergency requests, diagnosing problems and implementing solutions to restore system functionality.
  • Document all service activities accurately and thoroughly, including inspection reports, work orders, and parts usage, and customer notes, using the Service Trade operations platform.
  • Work closely with Deficiency Sellers to provide detailed inspection reports, material needs, and other job-related notes, to prepare and deliver repair estimates in a timely manner
  • Interact professionally with clients to schedule work, discuss inspection findings, address any concerns or questions, and provide recommendations for system upgrades or improvements
  • Work closely with Service Coordinator(s) to optimize work orders, material requisitions, and job scheduling, focusing on efficiency, productivity, and customer satisfaction.
  • Maintain a clean and organized work environment, always adhering to safety guidelines, protocols, and procedures.

title: Manufacturing Quality Supervisor - 1st shift (GWY100)
description:

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Lead with Safety and Development: Foster a safe and productive work environment by mentoring and coaching our employees. You'll ensure adherence to policies and provide constructive feedback to help everyone thrive.
  • Champion 5S Standards: Maintain process conditions that align with our 5S standards, ensuring a clean, organized, and efficient workspace.

  • Empower Your Team: Develop your team members by enhancing their job skills and knowledge. You’ll manage training records and ensure everyone meets our training standards.

  • Flexible Support: Be ready to support our night shift when needed, contributing to our team's success during split shifts or on an intermittent monthly basis (25%).

Qualifications

description:
Auto Property Damage Claims Associate (February 2027 Start)

Position Overview

Plymouth Rock Assurance is seeking motivated, customer-focused candidates graduating in May 2027 to join our Auto Property Damage (Auto PD) Claims Unit, with an anticipated start date of June or July 2027.

The Auto Property Damage Claims Associate is responsible for investigating and managing auto property damage claims, evaluating liability, and working toward fair and timely claim resolutions. This entry-level opportunity is ideal for upcoming college graduates interested in building a career in the insurance industry.

The role requires a high level of customer service, patience, and professionalism in a fast-paced environment with significant phone interaction. Successful candidates will demonstrate strong communication, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, along with the ability to navigate challenging conversations professionally.

Target Start Date: June/July 2027

Target Candidates: Students graduating with a bachelor's degree in May 2027 who are available to begin full-time employment in June or July 2027. Previous claims experience is not required. Comparative negligence claims handling experience is a plus.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities

Policy Analysis

  • Investigate and interpret policy provisions, endorsements, and conditions to determine coverage for automobile property damage claims.
  • Identify and investigate contested coverage claims that may require a roundtable discussion.

Claim Investigation

  • Investigate auto accidents to assess liability by interviewing first- and third-party claimants, witnesses, investigating officers, and other relevant parties.
  • Secure and analyze pertinent records, documentation, and loss scene information to determine proximate cause, negligence, and damages.

Claims Management

  • Evaluate and adjust reserves as necessary.
  • Prepare dispatch instructions for field personnel to inspect vehicles.
  • Negotiate and settle claims within individual authority limits, seeking supervisor approval for claims exceeding authority or requiring additional guidance.
  • Maintain effective follow-up systems on pending files and communicate claim status to insureds, claimants, and brokers.
  • Act as an intermediary between the company, preferred vendors, and customers to resolve disputes.
  • Ensure compliance with privacy guidelines, applicable laws, and claims handling regulations.

Subrogation and Legal Handling

  • Investigate and initiate subrogation processes when applicable.
  • Handle and respond to Special Civil Part lawsuits or intercompany arbitrations related to auto property damage claims.

Administrative Duties

  • Manage a customer-focused phone environment by answering calls, returning voicemails, and responding to emails and text correspondence promptly.
  • Process incoming and outgoing mail in a timely manner and in accordance with state guidelines.
  • Complete other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Education

  • Bachelor's degree required; candidates graduating in May 2027 are encouraged to apply.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, organizational, analytical, and customer service skills.

title: UAS Trainer
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The UAS Trainer supports unmanned aircraft system flight operations, customer training, testing and evaluation, technology demonstrations, Red Force activities, mission planning, scenario-based exercises, and range operations at the Constellis Training Center and other authorized locations.

Candidates can be considered for UAS Trainer, UAS Instructor and UAS Mission Planner opportunities if eligible based on experience.

This is a hands-on operational position requiring sound aviation judgment, safe flight practices, and the ability to operate UAS in structured training and range environments. Depending on qualifications and mission requirements, the employee may serve as a pilot, instructor, evaluator, mission planner, observer, or range-support team member.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Conduct safe UAS flight operations in accordance with FAA regulations, CTC policies, range procedures, customer requirements, and applicable SOPs.
  • Plan and execute assigned missions, including preflight preparation, aircraft and equipment inspections, launch, flight operations, recovery, and post-flight procedures.
  • Operate assigned UAS platforms, ground control stations, payloads, mission-planning applications, communications equipment, and associated support systems.
  • Serve as a pilot or operator during customer training, technology demonstrations, testing and evaluation, Red Force activities, and scenario-based exercises.

  • Work Environment: Employment is considered CASUAL. There is no standard work environment as the location, duration, and schedule is likely to change month by month. There will be a standard agreement in place to layout compensation, hours allocated, and employee standards.

QUALIFICATIONS

Business Analysis Manager

The Business Analysis Manager is the primary link between the business and IT for incoming project work and production issues, and the leader of the Business Analyst (BA) team. This role owns project intake and incident tracking, serves as the face of the BA team to business stakeholders, project managers, and IT leadership, and guides, develops, and supports a team of BAs to deliver maximum business value through effective systems analysis, requirements gathering, and process improvement.

The Business Analysis Manager works closely with senior business and IT leadership to prioritize projects, allocate resources, and drive continuous improvement in the BA function. This position requires exceptional communication skills, deep analytical expertise, and the resilience to navigate complex projects with patience, diplomacy, and focus.

This is a high-volume, fast-paced environment with constant competing demands. The ideal candidate stays calm and organized under pressure, tracks many projects and issues at once, and is self-motivated to keep work moving without waiting to be asked.

Key Responsibilities

Project Intake & Incident Tracking (Primary focus)

  • Manage the intake process for new project requests and enhancements: log, evaluate, and prioritize incoming work.
  • Partner with business stakeholders, project managers, and IT leadership to define scope, objectives, and success criteria for incoming initiatives.
  • Assign BA resources to initiatives based on priority, skills, and capacity.
  • Maintain a clear, current worklist of projects, issues, and priorities for the BA and development teams.
  • Triage, log, and coordinate the response to production work orders and incidents; track each through resolution and keep stakeholders informed.
  • Coordinate project estimation with development teams and deliver cost estimates to stakeholders once requirements are complete.
  • Gather dependency information from development teams and project managers to support project schedules.
  • Assist in tracking budget spend across the development teams and advise development managers of potential issues.

Business Communication & Team Representation

  • Serve as the face of the BA team and the centralized point of contact for project managers and business stakeholders on resource availability, project status, and incident updates.
  • Represent project and incident status in meetings with stakeholders and leadership.
  • Work with senior business and IT leadership to align priorities, set expectations, and communicate scope, trade-offs, and risks clearly.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams (Development, QA, UAT, Infrastructure) to align solutions with business objectives.
  • Coordinate with vendors, including Comparative Rater providers, to manage deliverables and maintain productive partnerships.

Team Management & Development

  • Lead, mentor, and coach a team of Business Analysts to enhance skills, consistency, and performance.
  • Recruit, develop, and retain top talent, managing performance through regular feedback and formal reviews.
  • Provide training and professional development opportunities for BAs and programmers.
  • Establish, maintain, and champion standards, methods, and best practices for business analysis across the organization.

Business Analysis Quality & Continuous Improvement

  • Oversee requirements elicitation, impact analysis, and documentation for new systems and enhancements to existing systems.
  • Perform workflow analysis, develop workflow diagrams, and recommend process improvements by defining “current state” and “future state” systems.
  • Ensure compliance with established standards and practices to deliver high-quality outcomes.
  • Collect, analyze, and share key performance metrics to drive improvements in BA processes.
  • Demonstrate and implement innovative approaches that shorten delivery cycles, reduce rework, and improve system capabilities.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, or Management Information Systems (or equivalent experience).
  • 15+ years of experience in the software development lifecycle, with a strong background in Business Analysis for IT-driven projects.
  • Experience leading, mentoring, or developing Business Analysts or similar technical staff.
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills to work effectively with diverse stakeholders and evolving priorities.
  • Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple projects, incidents, and shifting priorities simultaneously while maintaining accuracy and follow-through.
  • Ability to remain composed, professional, and effective in a high-pressure, high-volume environment.
  • Self-motivated and proactive, with a strong sense of ownership and urgency.
  • Ability to work on site in Boston, MA four days per week (required).
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.

Preferred:

  • Highly desirable: INS and CPCU certifications.
  • Highly desirable: Knowledge of APIs, web services, and related technologies (SQL, XML, HTML, XSLT, JSON) and tools such as Postman, REST API, and SoapUI.
  • 10+ years of BA experience in the Property & Casualty Insurance domain.
  • Project Management or related certifications.
  • Experience with web analytics tools such as Adobe Analytics, Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, FullStory, and Heap.
  • IIBA CBAP and AAC certifications (a plus).

title: PSS / Designated Defensive Marksman (PSS/DDM) | WPSIII
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Provide mobile armed personal protection and emergency response security services in high-risk areas for the Department of State in Baghdad, Iraq. Employees rotate in and out of country throughout the duration of their contract.

RESPONSIBILITIES

This list of duties and responsibilities is not intended to be all-inclusive and may be expanded to include other duties or responsibilities that management may deem necessary from time to time.

  • Provide designated defensive marksman services as assigned
  • Perform day-to-day personal protective security functions.
  • Drive the lead vehicle, principal’s vehicle, follow-vehicle, and/or act as response agent whenever required in motorcade or similar operations.
  • Carry and operate weapons as specified in daily post and detail orders, or upon orders from your chain of command
  • Participate in advance security preparations.
  • Man the security post at the principal’s residence, the command post, or other static post as required.
  • Serve as a member of a QRF as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Must be a U.S. citizen
  • Must currently possess a valid U.S. driver's license and a valid U.S. tourist passport to be considered
  • Must be 21 years of age or older
  • Must possess a minimum of three (3) years of documented protective security experience. A Service-2 or Member-4 copy of the DD-214 must be provided for applicants using U.S military service as applicable experience.
    • Protective security experience is defined as a personal bodyguard, a designated security member of convoy or movement operations, or security services experience while actively carrying a firearm. Experience may only be gained by employment under a national/federal government, state government, city/municipal government, provincial or township government, or a government-licensed commercial entity that provides armed protective services. Experience as sworn law enforcement in the United States is always applicable.
    • A minimum of two (2) years of this experience must be as a DDM/sniper Candidates claiming military experience must have either a sniper military occupation specialty (MOS) or additional skill identifier (ASI). If claiming law enforcement experience for this requirement, it must be full-time and not as a collateral duty.
  • Obtain and maintain a personnel security clearance as identified in the contract (DOS Secret level). Clearance can be obtained during the application process.
  • Must attend and successfully complete a sniper program issued by a military, or FBI training program. This sniper program must be of suitable complexity and quality to adequately prepare the graduate for successful performance as a WPS III DDM. Examples of programs that meet this requirement include, but are not limited to:
  1. United States Marine Corps (USMC) Scout/Sniper
  2. United States Army Sniper School

title: Field Network Engineer
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Constellis is seeking an experienced Field Network Engineer to support the Layered Extended Security Operations (LEXSO™) program. The engineer will work remotely when not supporting field activities but must be prepared to travel frequently to customer sites, test locations, demonstrations, installations, and other LEXSO operational environments. Travel requirements may vary significantly based on deployment schedules and customer needs.

LEXSO is an advanced, sensor-agnostic security technology platform that integrates sensors, communications, edge computing, networking, and automation into a unified operational environment. The platform is designed to integrate existing and new technologies into scalable architectures supporting critical infrastructure, defense, government, and other high-value facilities.

We are looking for a technically strong, hands-on engineer who is equally comfortable configuring a managed switch, troubleshooting a VLAN, installing and testing copper or fiber infrastructure, installing a sensor in the field, configuring a communications link, or working inside a server rack. The successful candidate must be capable of deploying to customer and test locations, working independently or as part of a small technical team, and troubleshooting complex systems under real-world field conditions.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Design, configure, deploy, and troubleshoot IP networks supporting LEXSO systems.
  • Install and configure routers, managed switches, firewalls, wireless systems, VPNs, and other network infrastructure.
  • Establish and maintain connectivity between sensors, servers, edge-compute systems, communications equipment, and the LEXSO platform.
  • Configure and troubleshoot VLANs, subnets, routing, DHCP, DNS, NAT, VPNs, firewall rules, and related network services.
  • Install, test, troubleshoot, and maintain copper and fiber-optic network infrastructure used to connect sensors, communications systems, compute infrastructure, and remote field equipment.
  • Work with single-mode and multimode fiber, SFP/SFP+ transceivers, media converters, fiber patch panels, and associated optical networking equipment.
  • Perform fiber troubleshooting using appropriate test equipment and understand common causes of optical-link degradation and failure.
  • Integrate field sensors including IP cameras, radar, LiDAR, unattended ground sensors, UAS/drone systems, counter-UAS systems, environmental sensors, and other IP-connected devices.
  • Install, configure, cable, and troubleshoot server racks, compute nodes, UPS systems, network appliances, patch panels, and associated infrastructure.
  • Support terrestrial, cellular, wireless, microwave, fiber-optic, and satellite communications used to connect distributed LEXSO systems.
  • Perform structured network troubleshooting using packet captures, network analysis tools, device logs, command-line utilities, and vendor diagnostic tools.
  • Diagnose connectivity, latency, packet loss, multicast, bandwidth, addressing, optical-link, power, and physical-layer issues.
  • Conduct site surveys and help develop network, communications, power, fiber, and equipment-placement plans for new deployments.
  • Configure equipment in laboratory and staging environments before field deployment.
  • Perform equipment installation, commissioning, operational testing, troubleshooting, and acceptance activities at customer sites.
  • Document network architectures, IP addressing, VLANs, equipment configurations, rack layouts, fiber and copper cable paths, and field changes.
  • Maintain accurate configuration records and deployment documentation.
  • Coordinate directly with software engineers, DevOps, sensor-integration engineers, field operations personnel, vendors, and customer technical teams.
  • Support demonstrations, operational exercises, system testing, and rapid deployments.
  • Identify field problems, determine root cause, implement corrective actions, and clearly communicate findings to the engineering team.
  • Provide remote technical support and troubleshooting for deployed LEXSO systems between field assignments.
  • Business work hours are Monday-Friday standard core hours, however some extended or weekend hours may be required.
  • Both domestic and international travel required for this role up to 60%

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Demonstrated 7 years of experience with enterprise and field-based IP networking environments.
  • Proven ability to configure, maintain, and troubleshoot Layer 2 and Layer 3 network infrastructure.
  • Strong understanding of VLANs, routing, switching, subnetting, DHCP, DNS, NAT, VPNs, and firewall technologies.
  • Experience deploying and supporting managed Ethernet switches and routers.
  • Knowledge of copper and fiber-optic Ethernet infrastructure, including installation and maintenance best practices.
  • Familiarity with both single-mode and multimode fiber-optic systems and their applications.
  • Experience working with SFP and SFP+ transceivers, optical links, fiber patching, connectors, and fiber distribution equipment.
  • Ability to install, inspect, clean, test, and troubleshoot fiber-optic cabling and related components.
  • Proficiency using fiber test equipment, including optical power meters, visual fault locators (VFLs), and optical time-domain reflectometers (OTDRs).
  • Experience utilizing network testing and diagnostic tools to identify and resolve connectivity and performance issues.
  • Working knowledge of Wireshark or comparable packet analysis tools for network troubleshooting and traffic analysis.
  • Strong understanding of TCP/IP and UDP-based networking systems and protocols.
  • Experience supporting wireless networking solutions and point-to-point communication systems.
  • Familiarity with secure remote access technologies, including WireGuard, IPsec, and other VPN solutions.
  • Proficiency with Linux operating systems and command-line based troubleshooting techniques.
  • Experience installing and configuring server racks, network racks, and associated infrastructure.
  • Knowledge of UPS systems and power distribution equipment supporting critical IT environments.
  • Experience integrating and supporting IP-based cameras, sensors, IoT devices, and other network-connected field equipment.
  • Ability to read, create, and maintain network diagrams, rack diagrams, wiring schematics, fiber maps, and technical documentation.
  • Preferred experience:
    • Physical security systems and security-system integration.
    • Surveillance camera and video-management systems.
    • Radar and LiDAR systems.
    • UAS or counter-UAS technologies.
    • Unattended ground sensors.
    • Satellite communications, including Starlink or similar systems.
    • Microwave or point-to-point wireless communications.
    • Cellular communications and multi-WAN networking.
    • Fiber-optic backbone and long-distance communications infrastructure.
    • Fiber termination, fusion splicing, OTDR testing, and optical-link troubleshooting.
    • Edge computing and GPU/server infrastructure.
    • Industrial or critical-infrastructure networking.
    • Government or Department of Defense environments.
    • Remote-site networking and communications.
    • Network monitoring and observability.
    • High-availability and redundant network architectures.
    • Portable or rapidly deployable communications systems.

BENEFITS

Constellis offers a comprehensive, total rewards package that includes competitive compensation and a flexible benefits package that reflects its commitment to creating a diverse and supportive workplace.

title: Manager, IT Service Desk
description:
JOB SUMMARY
The Manager, IT Service Desk serves as a strategic leader accountable for overseeing and advancing all aspects of technical support operations. This position requires a combination of technical proficiency, leadership, and a commitment to customer satisfaction. The ideal candidate will promote operational excellence, drive innovation, and consistently deliver high-quality IT services support across the organization.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES
Leadership and Strategy
  • Build and maintain a high-performance team by recruiting, developing, and mentoring skilled and motivated professionals in a collaborative environment that fosters a culture of excellence, teamwork, innovation, and continuous improvement.

  • Resolve conflicts effectively, fostering a positive and open environment where team members feel comfortable raising concerns and collaborating on solutions.
  • Demonstrate strong decision-making skills by analyzing information, weighing options, and making sound decisions that benefit the team and the organization.
  • Demonstrate adaptability and resilience by navigating change, unforeseen challenges, and tight deadlines calmly and confidently while maintaining a positive and proactive approach.

  • Train team members to recognize suspicious activity and events and ensure expeditious escalation and resolution of security incidents.
