title: Research Associate II, Technical Operations
description:
A-Alpha Bio is an early-stage, rapidly growing biotechnology platform company headquartered in Seattle, WA. We are focused on building the foundational data layer for AI-driven protein engineering. We provide biopharma companies and model builders with access to ground truth experimental datasets, including affinity and structure, for training, benchmarking and validating AI protein models. In parallel, we apply our data and models directly with select partners to engineer next-generation dual-specific and molecular glue therapeutics, and to discover and optimize differentiated biologics.

This role is not open to remote applicants and would require relocation to Seattle, WA.

Starting Salary Range: $75,000 - $88,000 annually

Exemption Status: Exempt

Location Expectations: Onsite

Reporting To: Manager II, Technical Operations

Role Description

A-Alpha Bio is seeking a Research Associate II to support our Technical Operations team’s execution of our AlphaSeq assay. In this role, you’ll execute DNA and yeast library construction, matings, next-generation sequencing, cell sorting, and flow cytometry to support interrogation of protein-protein interactions. Ideal candidates will have strong organizational skills, impeccable attention to detail, and an interest in executing screening assays at scale.

Key Responsibilities

  • Execute DNA library construction.
  • Perform yeast transformation and matings, cell sorting, and flow cytometry.
  • Execute DNA library preparation and sequencing workflows for Oxford Nanopore Technologies and Illumina platforms.
  • Support the development and optimization of standard operating procedures for existing and new experimental workflows.
  • Develop a foundational understanding of and executional expertise in Technical Operations methods.
  • May contribute to project teams, execute project-related tasks, and/or train new Research Associates.

Qualifications & Experience

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field with 2+ years of relevant postbaccalaureate laboratory experience in the biotechnology industry; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Proficiency in standard molecular biology techniques, including DNA extractions, quantitative PCR, Gibson assembly, and fragment analysis.
  • Experience with multi-parametric flow cytometry.
  • Experience in a high-throughput screening or manufacturing environment.
  • Experience working within a LIMS/ELN.
  • Strong work ethic, good organizational skills, team orientation, and exquisite attention to detail.
  • Flexibility in day-to-day schedule and willingness to work outside of standard hours when necessary, including weekends.

Preferred

  • Operator experience in a regulated environment (CLIA, cGXP, etc.).
  • Hands-on experience with Illumina or ONT NGS platforms.
  • Experience with cell sorting.
  • Experience using yeast as a model organism.
  • Experience with Benchling as a platform.
  • Experience using lab automation.

In 2018, A-Alpha Bio spun out of the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design and Center for Synthetic Biology – both communities filled with brilliant and highly entrepreneurial scientists. Since the company’s inception, we have built and scaled AlphaSeq, our high-throughput platform for quantitatively measuring protein-protein interactions at unprecedented scale. What began as a technology for generating large, standardized affinity datasets has grown into a broader data engine for AI-driven protein engineering. New members of the team should expect a fast-paced, highly dynamic, and interdisciplinary work environment. We are building a diverse, meritocratic, and supportive team that shares our values of speaking the truth, shooting for the moon, taking the reins, playing for the team, and improving the world.

A-Alpha Bio is headquartered in a custom designed lab and office space in downtown Seattle’s Belltown neighborhood. We are fortunate to be situated in a region that is renowned for its premier outdoor activities, including hiking, biking, climbing, skiing, kayaking, sailing, and more. At A-Alpha, you’ll find many who love the outdoors, but also gamers, amateur chefs, explorers, sports fans, bakers, crafters, photographers, brewers, jetsetters, animal lovers, and artists. Whatever your passions, you belong at A-Alpha Bio!

title: Operations Lead
description:
ABOUT US

JOB SUMMARY
The Operations Lead ensures that the club delivers an outstanding member experience every day by working closely with the General Manager and a team of club attendants and sales and service advisors to support daily operations, facility upkeep, and member service. In this role, the Operations Lead is responsible for maintaining a clean and safe environment, directing team members, monitoring member feedback, driving membership and retail revenue growth, and serving as Manager on Duty during assigned shifts. Through modeling our service promise and leading by example, the Operations Lead fosters a positive, results oriented culture focused on member satisfaction and strong business performance.

title: Vice President, Policy and Advocacy
description:
THE ORGANIZATION

The Charter School Growth Fund (CSGF) is a leading nonprofit venture philanthropy fund dedicated to identifying the nation’s best public charter schools, investing in their expansion, and helping to increase their impact. Our “portfolio” includes 200+ charter school networks that operate 1,700+ schools and serve more than 800,000 students. We are committed to expanding the impact of schools that are closing achievement and opportunity gaps. CSGF operates with the same strategies, discipline, and focus as a venture capital firm by awarding multi-year grants and loans to talented education entrepreneurs building networks of high-quality charter schools that enroll traditionally underserved students. Our goal is to serve 1,000,000 students by 2030 and 1.4 million by 2035.

This is an exciting time to join the Charter School Growth Fund. We are launching Fund V, our most ambitious fund yet, building on our 20-year track record of success. Fund V will add 250,000 new high-quality seats while helping our portfolio become durable, bedrock institutions in their communities for decades to come. We invest in the strongest charter leaders and networks in the country, and we partner closely with them to sustain excellent outcomes as they grow. Our portfolio continues to serve student populations of roughly 90% students of color and 75% students from low-income backgrounds, and we remain committed to being proximate to the lived experiences of the students and communities we serve.

THE OPPORTUNITY

CSGF is seeking a Vice President, Policy & Advocacy to join our Policy, Communications and Advocacy (PCA) team. Reporting to the Managing Director, PCA, the Vice President, Policy & Advocacy sets the vision for and drives CSGF’s portfolio advocacy strategy across a region of 15+ states. As an embedded expert on a Partner-led regional team, this Vice President serves as the primary advocacy and policy thought partner to portfolio members, regional Relationship Managers, and the Impact team — building durable advocacy capacity in portfolio networks and driving high-impact grassroots, coalition, and policy strategies that advance the charter sector.

This is a Vice President-level individual contributor role with no direct reports. The ideal candidate brings demonstrated expertise in advocacy, policy, and issues-based campaigns, with a proven ability to set a vision and strategy, secure buy-in from others, own outcomes, and influence senior leaders and diverse stakeholders — internal and external — across complex, multi-stakeholder environments. They are actively sought out for their expertise by portfolio members, state and local advocacy partners, and CSGF leadership, and are skilled at translating advocacy strategy into practical capacity-building support for charter school leaders.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Set and Drive Regional Advocacy Strategy (approximately 40%)

  • Set the vision for CSGF’s advocacy and policy strategy across a region of 15+ states, secure buy-in from regional and organizational leadership, and drive that strategy while owning outcomes and ensuring alignment with CSGF’s organizational goals and Fund V priorities.
  • Lead investment recommendations for advocacy grants and contracts, bringing the analysis and strategic rationale for Managing Director approval and setting clear, ambitious outcome expectations for each investment.
  • Set and lead the Policy and Advocacy Community of Practice learning agenda; develop, curate, and disseminate policy and advocacy resources to portfolio members through CSGF’s Seminar platform.
  • Identify complex advocacy threats and opportunities across the region before they arise; develop solutions, bring recommendations to the Managing Director and regional Partner, and proactively tackle issues that extend across the broader CSGF portfolio and organization.
  • Own the alignment of state-level policy and advocacy efforts with CSGF’s organizational goals, partner engagement strategies, and regional team priorities, and manage upward to ensure the regional team meets ambitious outcomes.

Serve as Advocacy Thought Partner to Regional Teams and Portfolio Members (approximately 40%)

  • Act as a primary advocacy and policy subject matter expert on the Partner-led regional team, providing strategic counsel to Partners, Relationship Managers, and the Impact team as they support portfolio members.
  • Serve as a trusted thought partner to portfolio member leaders on advocacy strategy, grassroots organizing, and coalition-building — building their capacity to lead effective advocacy efforts independently over time.
  • Identify and assess portfolio members’ evolving advocacy needs; maintain strong relationships with portfolio members that position CSGF as an actively sought-out resource at the state and local level.
  • Design and implement advocacy training and technical assistance for portfolio members; develop frameworks, tools, and resources that raise the floor of advocacy capability across the regional portfolio.
  • Design and lead grassroots and coalition-based advocacy strategies that mobilize portfolio leaders toward meaningful, measurable advocacy action.

Represent CSGF and Build the Regional Advocacy Ecosystem (approximately 20%)

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with state and local advocacy partners, coalitions, and policy stakeholders that advance CSGF’s regional strategy.
  • Represent CSGF externally in key state and local advocacy settings and with broader key stakeholders; grow CSGF’s credibility and influence with advocacy partners and policymakers in the region and begin to influence external parties to take action.
  • Identify, engage, and manage external consultants and advocacy partners as needed; set clear expectations and hold vendors accountable to quality and strategic alignment.
  • Contribute to CSGF’s broader PCA team strategy by sharing regional insights, synthesizing lessons learned, and informing organization-wide advocacy approaches; share working knowledge of advocacy and policy with colleagues across CSGF.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Skills and Characteristics

  • Deep commitment to CSGF’s mission and passion for K–12 education reform and charter sector advocacy
  • Demonstrated ability to set a vision and establish and drive advocacy strategy independently, securing buy-in from others and owning outcomes across complex, multi-stakeholder environments
  • Proven track record of building and maintaining strong relationships with diverse stakeholder groups — including elected officials, coalition partners, and charter school leaders — and of being sought out by them as a trusted resource and influencing them toward shared goals
  • Skilled at serving as a trusted thought partner to senior leaders and comfortable raising difficult issues with them; brings calm, strategic counsel that is actively sought out by those they advise
  • Exceptional interpersonal and written/verbal communication skills; effectively motivates and influences peers, senior leadership, and external stakeholders to take action in service of shared goals
  • Outstanding project management skills; demonstrated ability to see the strategic picture while managing execution details across multiple simultaneous workstreams and setting clear expectations for others, including senior leaders
  • Strong problem-solving and critical thinking skills; identifies complex issues before they arise, develops solutions, and proactively tackles issues that reach beyond their own function
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate politically complex environments with sophistication and nonpartisan credibility across the political spectrum
  • Demonstrated comfort making difficult decisions and working with ambiguity in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, including leading through changing circumstances
  • Ability to collaborate as an integral member of cross-functional regional teams; understands role as a specialist advisor and contributes proactively without overstepping relationship boundaries owned by Relationship Managers
  • Ability to travel up to 50% to support portfolio advocacy work, convenings, all-team gatherings, and in-person team and partner meetings

Educational Background and Work Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree required
  • 12+ years of progressive experience in advocacy, policy, electoral campaigns, or issues-based organizing, with a demonstrated portfolio of measurable impact — including setting and driving multi-state or multi-market advocacy strategies independently
  • Direct experience engaging executive and legislative branches of government at the state level; demonstrated ability to drive outcomes in complex political environment
  • Demonstrated experience building advocacy capacity in organizations, coalitions, or communities — not just executing campaigns, but leaving organizations stronger
  • Experience managing external consultants and advocacy partners; sets clear expectations and holds vendors accountable to quality and strategic alignment
  • Knowledge of charter school sector dynamics and education policy landscape strongly preferred; recognized as an expert in advocacy and policy beyond one's own organization
  • Direct knowledge and experience with state legislative processes required

COMPENSATION

Compensation is commensurate with experience and education. The target salary range for this role is $130,000-$160,000 annually. CSGF offers a very competitive package of benefits, including: health, life, disability, and dental insurance coverage; vacation/holidays and parental leave; and participation in CSGF’s 403(b) plan. Candidates must have permanent authorization to work in the US.

START DATE

CSGF is seeking candidates who can start as soon as possible; flexible for the ideal candidate.

WORKING AT CSGF

We are focused on hiring and developing great people and believe that building diverse perspectives across our team makes us more effective in expanding our impact. (This is reflected in Our Commitment Statement.) Our core values are:

Why you'll love working here:

  • Join a team driven by purpose, collaboration, and a commitment to identifying and responding to the needs of the public charter schools that we support
  • Access to professional development and learning opportunities

Our core values are:

Results

  • We believe that student success is the ultimate measure of our performance.
  • We work with urgency and intentionality for the portfolio and their schools.
  • We hold ourselves accountable to strong outcomes.
  • We relentlessly prioritize our resources to drive positive, measurable, attributable impact for the charter leaders, their schools, and ultimately students.
  • We believe strong results come from good decisions, and the best decisions are made when we use data - both quantitative and qualitative - and gather input from diverse perspectives, especially those most impacted by the work.
  • We celebrate our wins and learn from our losses.

Teamwork

  • We value organization over team, and we value team over individual.
  • We actively break down silos and collaborate across teams.
  • We believe building strong, healthy relationships is critical to move our work forward.
  • We seek to proactively communicate across teams to strengthen our outcomes and add value for the portfolio.

Integrity

  • We believe that trust is our most important asset, and we must earn and maintain the trust of the portfolio member leaders, investors, and our team to achieve our goals.
  • We are often entrusted with sensitive and confidential information about the portfolio - we do not ever violate these confidences.
  • We show ownership for our successes and our failures.
  • We speak directly to the person, even when it's messy and hard, and get ahead of potential problems.
  • We do the right thing, even when no one is watching.

Respect

  • We understand and acknowledge our place in the value chain – the students, teachers, principals, and other leaders at portfolio networks are doing the hardest, direct, and most impactful work in their schools each day.
  • We prioritize humility and embrace getting better every day.
  • We are curious and open-minded.
  • We are aware of our own biases and how they might affect our judgment, and we take ownership to mitigate their impact.

Entrepreneurship

  • We take calculated risks, looking for new ways to add value and improve how we work.
  • We are problem solvers in all aspects of our work.
  • We actively connect people and ideas in strategic ways to foster new ideas and learning.
  • We acknowledge not all investments will succeed and embrace failure as it facilitates deeper learning for our organization and the portfolio.

E-VERIFY STATEMENT

This employer participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. If E-Verify cannot confirm that you are authorized to work, this employer is required to give you written instructions and an opportunity to contact the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) or Social Security Administration (SSA) so you can begin to resolve the issue before the employer can take any action against you. Including terminating employment. Employers can only use E-Verify once you have accepted a job offer and completed the I-9 form.

title: Data Engineer Co-op - Homeowners Insurance
description:
Data Engineer Co-Op, Homeowners Insurance

The Plymouth Rock Home Group is an innovative Insurtech start-up within a successful, well-established insurance organization. We quadrupled topline revenue over the past 4 years by revolutionizing the way homeowners insurance is priced, marketed, bought, and sold. Our customers obtain a home insurance quote in seconds using our @Home quoting engine. But the fast quote is not the real innovation. We collect large, detailed data about homes, homeowners and where they are located. The @Home product uses cutting edge techniques from skilled data scientists across machine learning and artificial intelligence to create models that predict loss costs, likelihood to buy, the best service and coverages we can offer, and the best way to provide them.   • Automate data cataloging to improve data visibility and surface quality issues early

The Plymouth Rock Company and its affiliated group of companies write and manage over $1.8 billion in personal and commercial auto and homeowner’s insurance throughout the Northeast and mid-Atlantic, where we have built an unparalleled reputation for service. title: Technical Lead - Plant Operations
description:
Benefits:
  • 401(k) matching
  • Bonus based on performance
  • Dental insurance
  • Health insurance
  • Paid time off
  • Vision insurance

Who We Are

Auris Noble is a vertically integrated recovery and refining company that manages high-value critical and strategic materials generated by aerospace, defense, telecommunications, advanced manufacturing, and other industries. We develop science-driven solutions for recovering and upscaling complex and previously underserved material streams containing precious, refractory, rare earth, and strategic metals. Our capabilities span laboratory development, analytical chemistry, pilot operations, commercial-scale chemical processing, thermal treatment, metal recovery, and production of refined materials. Auris Noble operates multiple facilities and produces materials under an ISO 9001:2015 quality management system.

Position Overview

Serve as the hands-on operational leader for an assigned production or process area. At least two positions are expected to function substantially like plant or area managers, with responsibility for people, safety, production, quality, equipment readiness, cost, schedule, and delivery of assigned project objectives. Assignments may involve critical-material recovery, separation, purification, thermal processing, or product upscaling.

This position will lead one or more company growth programs involving facility expansion, process scale-up, equipment installation and commissioning, recovery and separation of complex critical material mixtures, and transition of new or improved processes into sustained production. Assignments will evolve by project phase and will include P&ID design, requirements development, vendor coordination, pilot trials, qualification, documentation, training, production support, and continuous improvement.

Position and Benefits

Auris Noble offers a full-time, on-site position with benefits that may include health, dental and vision insurance; paid time off and holidays; 401(k) matching; quarterly bonuses; annual profit sharing; and a planned annual plant shutdown, subject to plan terms and company policy.

Job Responsibilities

● Lead daily operations for an assigned plant area, production line, or technical workstream and maintain visible presence in the operating area.

● Set priorities and coordinate operators, technicians, engineers, chemists, maintenance personnel, quality staff, and contractors.

● Own area performance for safety, environmental compliance, production schedule, throughput, recovery, yield, purity, scrap, downtime, housekeeping, and cost.

● Develop staffing, shift, training, qualification, material, and equipment-readiness plans required to meet production and project targets.

● Lead daily or weekly operating meetings, assign actions, remove constraints, manage risks, and escalate decisions when needed.

● Participate in requirements definition, equipment specification, vendor review, installation, startup, commissioning, and qualification of new or modified systems.

● Ensure completion and use of SOPs, batch records, work instructions, preventive-maintenance plans, inspection records, and operating logs.

● Lead pilot and production campaigns, coordinate upstream and downstream work, review mass balances and analytical results, and freeze operating parameters for production release.

● Partner with ESH and quality personnel on hazard reviews, management of change, incident investigation, corrective action, audits, and process-quality objectives.

● Develop frontline employees through coaching, performance feedback, cross-training, and consistent accountability.

● Provide concise technical and operational status, schedule, risk, production, and quality information for program reports and leadership reviews.

Education, Training and Experience

● Bachelor's degree in engineering, chemistry, metallurgy, operations management, or a related field, or equivalent progressive industrial experience.

● 10+ years of chemical, metals, advanced materials, or comparable manufacturing experience, including direct leadership of production or technical teams.

● Demonstrated responsibility for plant or area safety, quality, production, maintenance coordination, staffing, and performance improvement.

● Experience with startup, commissioning, process scale-up, troubleshooting, and operation of industrial equipment.

● Ability to lead in both structured project settings and fast-moving plant environments.

Preferred Qualifications

● Experience managing multiple shifts or technically complex batch/continuous-processing operations.

● Background in hydrometallurgy, metal refining, inorganic chemical processing, thermal processing, or high-value materials.

● Experience with capital projects, IQ/OQ/PQ, preventive maintenance, ISO 9001, Lean/Six Sigma, or statistical process control.

● Prior responsibility for operating budgets, production planning, inventory, or contractor supervision.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

● Able to communicate clearly and effectively in writing and in person.

● Able to organize work, manage changing priorities, and collaborate across technical and business functions.

● Demonstrates sound judgment, attention to detail, initiative, and commitment to safe, ethical work.

● Proficient with Microsoft Office and able to learn company systems.

● Able to protect confidential, proprietary, customer, and controlled project information.

Work Environment and Other Requirements

● This is an on-site position and is not eligible for a fully remote work schedule.

● Work will require movement between offices, laboratories, production areas, warehouses, construction areas, and vendor sites.

● Must be able to wear required personal protective equipment and comply with chemical, industrial, and facility safety rules.

● Occasional travel, schedule flexibility, or work during commissioning and plant shutdown activities may be required.

● Must be a U.S. citizen due to project and contractual requirements.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Auris Noble LLC is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, consistent with applicable law. This description identifies the general nature and level of work expected and is not intended to contain every duty or responsibility. Responsibilities may evolve as company and project needs change.

title: Senior Power BI Data Engineer

title: UAS Technical Expert
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The UAS Technical Expert supports unmanned aircraft system flight operations, customer training, testing and evaluation, technology demonstrations, Red Force activities, mission planning, scenario-based exercises, and range operations at the Constellis Training Center and other authorized locations.

Candidates can be considered for UAS Trainer, UAS Instructor and UAS Mission Planner opportunities if eligible based on experience.

This is a hands-on operational position requiring sound aviation judgment, safe flight practices, and the ability to operate UAS in structured training and range environments. Depending on qualifications and mission requirements, the employee may serve as a pilot, instructor, evaluator, mission planner, observer, or range-support team member.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Conduct safe UAS flight operations in accordance with FAA regulations, CTC policies, range procedures, customer requirements, and applicable SOPs.
  • Plan and execute assigned missions, including preflight preparation, aircraft and equipment inspections, launch, flight operations, recovery, and post-flight procedures.
  • Operate assigned UAS platforms, ground control stations, payloads, mission-planning applications, communications equipment, and associated support systems.
  • Serve as a pilot or operator during customer training, technology demonstrations, testing and evaluation, Red Force activities, and scenario-based exercises.
  • Provide classroom and hands-on UAS instruction when assigned and qualified, including support for lesson plans, practical exercises, and student evaluations.
  • Support reconnaissance, surveillance, mapping, EO/IR, threat-replication, and other UAS-enabled mission requirements.
  • Assist with testing and evaluation of aircraft, payloads, sensors, software, communications systems, and emerging technologies, including test execution, observations, documentation, and after-action feedback.
  • Maintain required flight logs, training records, equipment records, and operational documentation.
  • Conduct authorized field-level inspections and troubleshooting and report equipment deficiencies, maintenance concerns, or unsafe conditions.
  • Support range preparation, equipment staging, safety procedures, launch and recovery operations, accountability, and coordination with customers, instructors, safety personnel, vendors, and range control.
  • Maintain proficiency on assigned systems and comply with all safety, security, communications, information-protection, and risk-management requirements.
  • Perform other UAS, training, testing, and range-support duties consistent with assigned qualifications.
  • Other duties as assigned.
  • Work Environment: Employment is considered CASUAL. There is no standard work environment as the location, duration, and schedule is likely to change month by month. There will be a standard agreement in place to layout compensation, hours allocated, and employee standards.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Current FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate.
  • At least one year of demonstrated UAS operational experience involving practical flight operations.
  • Working knowledge of UAS flight principles, mission planning, airspace requirements, weather considerations, inspections, emergency procedures, and operational risk management.
  • Ability to safely conduct preflight, launch, flight, recovery, and post-flight operations in a structured military, government, public-safety, commercial, training, or range environment.
  • Ability to follow technical instructions, test plans, range procedures, SOPs, and customer requirements while maintaining accurate operational records.
  • Ability to communicate professionally and work effectively with customers, instructors, safety personnel, and other operational staff.
  • Ability to work outdoors, handle UAS equipment, maintain a flexible or irregular schedule, and travel periodically when required.
  • Ability to satisfy applicable company, customer, background, and facility-access requirements.
  • Preferred:
    • Three or more years of UAS operational experience.
    • Prior UAS instructor, trainer, evaluator, military, government, public-safety, or range experience.
    • Experience operating multiple UAS platforms, including multirotor, fixed-wing, FPV, autonomous, or semi-autonomous systems.
    • Experience with EO/IR sensors, ISR, mapping, reconnaissance, or other specialized payloads.
    • Experience supporting Red Force activities, scenario-based training, testing and evaluation, or technology demonstrations.
    • Experience developing or implementing Programs of Instruction, lesson plans, SOPs, practical exercises, or evaluation criteria.
    • FAA, military, technical, or industry-recognized UAS training or certifications.
    • Current or previously held U.S. Government security clearance.
    • Equivalent military, aviation, law enforcement, public-safety, instructional, or technical experience may be considered where appropriate.

Employment Type: FTE
Working Mode: Hybrid (Travel Required)
Language: English
Start: November 9, 2026 – April 30, 2027

We are looking for an experienced Senior Data Engineer / Data Pipeline Architect for an assignment in Stockholm focusing on data pipeline modernization, data security, and technical architecture.

The assignment involves leading the technical migration of existing data pipelines to meet stricter requirements for encryption, data retention, and deletion of user data, including historical and derived datasets.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and drive the architecture, migrating pipelines incrementally while ensuring existing outputs remain unchanged.
  • Establish sustainable engineering processes for testing, code reviews, incident management, and releases.
  • Combine architectural leadership with hands‑on engineering using Airflow, Spark, dbt, BigQuery, and Python.
  • Collaborate closely with and mentor a Data Engineer within the team, ensuring long‑term ownership, reliability, and independent maintenance of the migrated pipelines.

Must-Have Requirements

  1. Minimum 5 years of relevant professional experience (5–10 years overall).
  2. Deep hands‑on experience with Airflow, Spark, dbt, BigQuery, and Python.
  3. Proven experience technically leading at least one complete data pipeline migration from start to finish.
  4. Experience refactoring production data pipelines while verifying that their outputs remain unchanged.
  5. Experience establishing and implementing engineering processes for testing, code reviews, and incident management.
  6. Demonstrated mentoring experience with measurable outcomes.

Education

  • Minimum Bachelor's degree (or equivalent).

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience with encryption at rest, data retention, or data deletion compliance (e.g., GDPR).
  • Experience with envelope encryption and key management solutions (e.g., GCP KMS, AEAD functions, or Tink).
  • Knowledge of BigQuery column-level security, policy tags, and Data Catalog.
  • Experience with Config Connector (KCC) for managing GCP resources through Kubernetes.
  • Experience with event-driven architectures using Kafka.

description:

Constellis offers a comprehensive, total rewards package that includes competitive compensation and a flexible benefits package that reflect its commitment to creating a diverse and supportive workplace.

title: Director, Comparative Rater Strategy & Analytics
description:
The Director, Comparative Rater Strategy & Analytics is responsible for leading comparative rater strategy and related competitive intelligence gathering, and analytics for Plymouth Rock’s Partners distribution channel.

This role leads comparative rater strategy, market intelligence, and business analytics into strategic assets that drive profitable growth, improve competitive positioning, and support data-driven decision making across Plymouth Rock's distribution organization. The Director serves as the primary business leader responsible for understanding how Plymouth Rock competes, performs, and grows across agency, partnership, and comparative rater distribution channels.

The position will partner closely with Product Management, Distribution, Marketing, IT, Operations, Underwriting, and Financial Planning to identify opportunities that improve growth, retention, profitability, agency productivity, and customer acquisition effectiveness.

This is a working management position requiring both strong leadership capabilities and the ability to personally conduct analyses, develop recommendations, and influence business decisions.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Comparative Rater Strategy & Optimization

  • Develop and execute Plymouth Rock's comparative rater strategy, including platform optimization, vendor management, implementation governance, and long-term roadmap planning.
  • Serve as the primary relationship owner with comparative rater vendors, driving improvements in quote performance, agent experience, carrier visibility, and operational efficiency.
  • Partner with Product, Underwriting, and IT teams to ensure product, rate, underwriting, and filing changes are accurately implemented across comparative rating platforms.
  • Lead optimization of comparative rater workflows, including eligibility rules, company-specific questions, defaults, quote return performance, carrier visibility logic, and quality assurance processes.
  • Monitor comparative rater performance and develop recommendations to improve agency adoption, quoting efficiency, and policy conversion.

Competitive Intelligence & Market Strategy

  • Lead Plymouth Rock's competitive intelligence efforts within the Partners distribution channel by monitoring pricing position, product competitiveness, quoting performance, market trends, and competitor activity. Collaborate with stakeholders in Product Management and IT to drive improvements in these results.
  • Develop competitive intelligence frameworks, dashboards, and executive reporting that benchmark Plymouth Rock's performance and identify opportunities to improve market share, profitability, and growth.
  • Analyze competitive positioning by state, product, agency segment, and distribution channel and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Monitor comparative rating technology, insurtech innovation, and emerging market trends while supporting Product and Distribution leadership in evaluating opportunities and threats.

Distribution Analytics & Business Performance

  • Deliver performance measurement, business intelligence, and decision support across partnership, agency, and comparative rater distribution channels.
  • Develop executive dashboards, KPI frameworks, and management reporting that measure growth, retention, profitability, agency productivity, customer acquisition effectiveness, and overall distribution performance.
  • Partner with Finance to optimize agency economics, compensation effectiveness, producer productivity, customer lifetime value, and channel profitability to support investment decisions and resource allocation.
  • Partner with Distribution, Product, and Marketing leadership to identify, prioritize, and execute initiatives that increase quote volume, policy growth, partner productivity, and distribution profitability.
  • Support business development efforts through partner evaluations, business case development, growth opportunity analysis, and strategic planning.
  • Ensure reporting accuracy, analytical consistency, data governance, and effective use of data across the organization.

Leadership & Stakeholder Management

  • Lead and develop a high-performing team responsible for comparative rater optimization, competitive intelligence, reporting, analytics, and business performance insights.
  • Establish priorities, allocate resources, and manage team workloads to support strategic business objectives.
  • Build strong partnerships across Product, Distribution, Marketing, Finance, IT, Operations, Underwriting, and Financial Planning teams.
  • Present findings, recommendations, and strategic initiatives to executive leadership and translate complex analytical findings into actionable business decisions.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Actuarial Science, Business Analytics, Computer Science, Finance, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in insurance analytics, competitive intelligence, distribution strategy, product management, pricing, business intelligence, or related disciplines.
  • Minimum 5 years of leadership experience managing analytical, strategic, or business performance teams.
  • Strong knowledge of personal lines insurance, agency distribution models, customer acquisition strategies, and channel economics.
  • Experience with comparative rating platforms such as Vertafore, EZLynx, PL Rating, EPIC, Bolt, or similar technologies preferred.
  • Advanced SQL proficiency and experience working with large-scale data environments.
  • Strong analytical and reporting skills utilizing Excel, Tableau, Power BI, SAS, Python, R, or similar tools.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence product, pricing, underwriting, marketing, and distribution strategies through analytical insights and business recommendations.
  • Exceptional communication, problem-solving, and strategic planning skills.

Key Success Metrics

  • Comparative rater quote volume growth
  • Quote-to-bind conversion performance
  • Share of #1 and Top 3 quote positions
  • Competitive positioning versus key market competitors
  • Independent and captive agency premium growth
  • Agency productivity and retention performance
  • Customer acquisition and conversion effectiveness
  • Distribution profitability and channel economics
  • Reporting accuracy and timeliness
  • Comparative rater implementation quality
  • Adoption and utilization of analytical insights
  • Executive stakeholder satisfaction

SALARY RANGE

The pay range for this position is $186,500 to $247,000 annually. Actual compensation will vary based on multiple factors, including employee knowledge and experience, role scope, business needs, geographical location, and internal equity.​

PERKS & BENEFITS

  • 4 weeks accrued paid time off, 8 paid national holidays per year, and 2 floating holidays
  • Low cost and excellent coverage health insurance options that start on Day 1 (medical, dental, vision)
  • Annual 401(k) Employer Contribution
  • Free onsite gym and health center at our Woodbridge Location
  • Resources to promote Professional Development (LinkedIn Learning and licensure assistance)
  • Robust health and wellness program and fitness reimbursements
  • Various Paid Family leave options including Paid Parental Leave
  • Tuition Reimbursement

ABOUT THE COMPANY

The Plymouth Rock Company and its affiliated group of companies write and manage over $2 billion in personal and commercial auto and homeowner’s insurance throughout the Northeast and mid-Atlantic, where we have built an unparalleled reputation for service. We continuously invest in technology, our employees thrive in our empowering environment, and our customers are among the most loyal in the industry. The Plymouth Rock group of companies employs more than 1,900 people and is headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. Plymouth Rock Assurance Corporation holds an A.M. Best rating of “A-/Excellent”.

  • Possesses basic comprehension and working knowledge of PLCs and automated systems.

  • Communicate technical issues to others and evaluate responses in a group setting.

Job Description:

Part-Time Local Sort Supervisor – Extended Bemidji, MN Center

Hours: Monday-Friday 4:00pm-9:00pm

Pay: $26.25/hour

Associates/bachelor's degree preferred but not required.


Position Summary

The Part-Time Local Sort Supervisor is responsible for overseeing the daily PM operations of the local sort within an extended UPS center. This position provides leadership and direction to hourly employees to ensure packages are processed safely, accurately, and efficiently while meeting established service commitments and operational goals.

The supervisor is responsible for coordinating staffing, managing workflow, monitoring productivity, ensuring compliance with UPS policies and procedures, and maintaining a safe and productive work environment. This role requires strong leadership, sound decision-making, effective communication, and the ability to adapt to changing operational demands in a fast-paced environment.


Key Responsibilities:

Operational Leadership

  • Direct and oversee daily local sort operations to ensure packages are processed accurately and within established service commitments.
  • Coordinate staffing, employee assignments, and work areas based on daily volume and operational needs.
  • Monitor package flow, production levels, and operational performance to identify and address inefficiencies.
  • Ensure proper handling, scanning, loading, and dispatch of packages.
  • Proactively identify operational challenges and implement solutions to maintain service and productivity.
  • Coordinate with the morning preload team, delivery drivers, feeder department, and other operational departments, as needed to ensure seamless communication and package movement.
  • Maintain operational accountability throughout the sort and ensure all assigned responsibilities are completed.

Safety and Compliance

  • Promote a strong safety culture by ensuring employees follow UPS safety policies, procedures, and safe work methods.
  • Conduct safety observations and address unsafe behaviors or working conditions.
  • Ensure employees receive appropriate training and understand their job responsibilities.
  • Maintain compliance with company policies, procedures, and applicable labor agreements.
  • Take immediate action to correct safety concerns and prevent workplace injuries.

Employee Leadership and Development

  • Provide daily direction, coaching, and feedback to hourly employees.
  • Establish clear performance expectations and hold employees accountable for meeting operational standards.
  • Recognize strong performance and identify opportunities for employee development.
  • Address attendance, performance, and conduct issues promptly and consistently.
  • Foster a positive, respectful, and productive work environment.
  • Build effective working relationships with employees, union representatives, and management.

Service and Performance Management

  • Monitor service performance and ensure all packages are processed to meet established commitments.
  • Review operational reports and performance indicators to identify trends and improvement opportunities.
  • Address service failures, misloads, package exceptions, and other operational concerns.
  • Ensure proper communication and follow-up on unresolved operational issues.
  • Drive continuous improvement in productivity, efficiency, service, and employee performance.

Communication and Administrative Responsibilities

  • Communicate operational expectations, staffing needs, and performance updates to management.
  • Maintain accurate operational records and complete required reports and documentation.
  • Communicate effectively with employees and management regarding daily operational changes and expectations.
  • Exercise sound judgment when addressing employee concerns and operational challenges.
  • Ensure appropriate communication and coordination between departments within the extended center.

Qualifications and Skills

  • Demonstrated leadership and supervisory abilities.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced operational environment.
  • Knowledge of package handling operations and UPS procedures preferred.
  • Ability to analyze operational performance and implement corrective actions.
  • Ability to hold employees accountable while maintaining positive working relationships.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Commitment to safety, service, and operational excellence.

Core Leadership Expectations

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Accountability: Takes ownership of operational results and follows through on commitments.
  • Leadership: Sets clear expectations, leads by example, and develops employees.
  • Safety: Makes safety the highest priority in all operational decisions.
  • Communication: Provides clear, timely, and consistent direction.
  • Adaptability: Responds effectively to changing volume, staffing, and operational demands.
  • Integrity: Demonstrates professionalism, consistency, and sound judgment.
  • Results Orientation: Drives performance while balancing safety, service, and employee engagement.

Overall Performance Expectations

The Part-Time Local Sort Supervisor is expected to lead a safe, efficient, and service-oriented operation while developing employee capability and maintaining accountability. Success in this role is measured through safety performance, service execution, productivity, employee engagement, operational compliance, and the ability to consistently meet the needs of the extended center.

Permanent

Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several US geographic markets. The base pay for this position ranges from $26.25/hr to $42.65/hr. We are seeking a highly skilled and visionary Platform Architect to join our technology team. This role is responsible for designing, implementing, and governing enterprise platform solutions that enable scalable, secure, and resilient business applications across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments. As the subject matter expert and escalation point, you will drive architecture standards, deliver strategic projects, and partner with engineering, operations, and business stakeholders to ensure our platforms support innovation, compliance, and operational excellence.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities:

Architecture, Design & Standards

  • Own end-to-end platform architecture (cloud, on-prem, hybrid), including infrastructure, middleware, network, telecom, integration patterns, and automation frameworks.
  • Define, document, and enforce configuration standards, security controls, versioning, and compliance policies across platforms and environments.
  • Develop standards system documentation artifacts such as High-Level Diagrams, Low-Level Diagrams, Data Flow diagrams, SOPs etc. to ensure consistent documentation across the platforms.
  • Lead solution design for platform solutions including but not exclusive to resiliency, automation, and observability.
  • Evaluate and select platform technologies, tools, and patterns aligned with enterprise strategy and best practices.
  • Partner closely with the Enterprise Architecture team to align platform designs with enterprise architecture principles, reference architectures, and long-term technology strategy.
  • Collaborate with the Security team to embed security-by-design, threat modeling, identity, access controls, and compliance requirements into all platform architectures and standards.
  • Work in alignment with DevOps teams to define and standardize CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code patterns, automation frameworks, and operational best practices.
  • Participate in and contribute to architecture review boards to review and approve platform designs and standards.

Implementation, Operations & Tier 4 Support

  • Provide Tier 4 diagnostics and resolution for complex platform incidents (infrastructure, middleware, automation, security).
  • Help develop solutions to configure, monitor and troubleshoot using platform-native and third-party tools (e.g., Terraform, Kubernetes, AWS, Prometheus, Grafana).

Platform Integrations & Enablement

  • Design and optimize integration flows, self-service capabilities, and developer experience outcomes.
  • Oversee integration with business applications, third-party services, and internal tools; enable extensibility and automation.
  • Provide program leadership for platform adoption, track roadmaps, SLAs, and usage metrics.

Governance, Documentation & Collaboration

  • Maintain comprehensive runbooks, SOPs, diagrams, and inventories (infrastructure maps, API catalogs, security policies).
  • Deliver technical/admin training and knowledge transfer to engineering, operations, and business teams.
  • Partner with Network, Security, Middleware, System, Database, DevOps, Operations, Service Desk, PMO, and Application teams to ensure secure, scalable, and integrated platform services.

Qualifications and Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or equivalent experience.
  • 5-10 years in platform architecture, infrastructure engineering, and platform operations.
  • Demonstrated breadth across platform domains: cloud, on-prem, hybrid, automation, integration, security as well as different workloads (OLAP, OLTP, batch)
  • Strong experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), container orchestration (Kubernetes, Docker), and infrastructure as code (Terraform, Ansible).
  • Hands-on with CI/CD, API gateways, service mesh, monitoring/logging platforms.
  • Expertise in platform security, compliance, and audit readiness.
  • Practical knowledge of integration technologies (REST, GraphQL, event-driven), automation frameworks, and developer enablement.
  • Networking fundamentals for platforms: TCP/IP, DNS, load balancing, firewalls, VPNs.
  • Excellent communication, documentation, stakeholder engagement, and vendor management skills.
  • Experience with platform governance, policy enforcement, and operational best practices.
  • Familiarity with ITIL framework

Salary Range: $135,000-$180,000 per year. Actual compensation will vary based on multiple factors, including employee knowledge and experience, role scope, business needs, geographical location, and internal equity.

title: Sr Cyber Security Engineer
description:
Position Overview

The Senior Cyber Security Engineer will bridge the gap between "Compliance" and "Engineering." You will not just audit the system, you will help build it securely and own the cybersecurity workstream end-to-end. This role is responsible for achieving Authority to Operate (ATO) under DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) standards among other federal certifications while embedding security automation directly into our CI/CD pipelines, and reporting program status and risk directly to LEXSO leadership. You will work side-by-side with backend and frontend engineers to harden the microservices architecture against evolving threats, and you will independently identify security gaps, drive architectural design decisions and shepherd remediation to completion..

Responsibilities

  • Own the LEXSO cybersecurity program end-to-end – from gap identification through architectural design to implementation tracking
  • Report cyber risk posture and remediation progress; translate technical findings into terms leadership can act on
  • Define and maintain the cybersecurity requirements backlog and progress-tracking cadence
  • Lead the technical execution of the RMF process to achieve and maintain Authority to Operate (ATO) for the LEXSO platform
  • Implement security controls in accordance with NIST SP 800-53 and DoD SRG/STIGs
  • Generate and maintain artifacts required for eMASS, including SSPs, POAMs, and SARs
  • Conduct self-assessments using ACAS (Nessus) and SCAP Compliance Checker (SCC) to identify vulnerabilities
  • Integrate automated security testing (SAST/DAST) tools (e.g., SonarQube, OWASP ZAP) into the GitLab/GitHub CI/CD pipeline
  • Develop scripts (Python, Bash, Ansible) to automate patching and configuration management for Linux (RHEL/Ubuntu) servers
  • Implement Container Security scanning for Docker/Kubernetes environments to detect vulnerabilities before deployment
  • Enforce "Security as Code" principles using Terraform or Helm charts
  • Analyze vulnerability scan results and write the code/scripts to remediate findings (e.g., fixing SSH configurations, patching libraries, hardening NGINX)
  • Harden APIs and microservices by implementing secure authentication (OAuth2/JWT/mTLS) and encryption standards (FIPS 140-2)
  • Respond to zero-day threats and CVEs by rapidly deploying hotfixes to the production environment
  • Conduct threat modeling sessions with the engineering team to identify attack vectors in the multi-sensor architecture
  • Design and implement secure logging and auditing pipelines (ELK Stack/Splunk) to meet audit requirements
  • Advise on the secure architecture for integrating third-party sensors (LiDAR, Radar) and IoT devices
  • Work is typically based in a remote working environment and subject to frequent interruptions. Business work hours are Monday-Friday from 8:00 am to 5:00 pm, however some extended or weekend hours may be required.
  • Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in Cyber Security Engineering or DevSecOps.
  • Proven track record of achieving ATO (Authority to Operate) for a software system in a DoD/Federal environment
  • Hands-on experience with RMF, NIST 800-53, and DISA STIGs
  • Proficiency in scripting languages (Python, Bash) for automation
  • Experience with vulnerability scanning tools (ACAS/Nessus, SonarQube, Burp Suite)
  • Strong knowledge of Linux Security (SELinux, iptables, hardening)
  • Experience with CI/CD tools (GitLab CI, Jenkins) and Container Security (Docker/K8s)
  • Demonstrated ability to work autonomously — identify security gaps, drive architectural design decisions, and track implementation through to completion
  • Experience communicating technical findings and program status to executive leadership; able to translate risk and remediation into terms leadership can act on
  • Track record of ownership over requirements definition and progress reporting for cybersecurity workstreams
  • CISSP, CASP+, or Security+ CE (Required)
  • Active Secret Security Clearance
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cyber Security, or related technical discipline.
  • Preferred Experience:
    • Experience securing cloud environments (AWS GovCloud / Azure Government)
    • Experience with FedRAMP authorization processes
    • Familiarity with "Zero Trust" architecture principles
    • Previous experience as a Software Developer before moving into Security
    • Prior experience as a technical lead or senior individual contributor with direct exposure to stakeholders

BENEFITS

Constellis offers a comprehensive, total rewards package that includes competitive compensation and a flexible benefits package that reflect its commitment to creating a diverse and supportive workplace.

title: Senior Specialist (Product Scale-up), Global Manufacturing
description:
Role and impact

How do you help a new catalyst product move from development towards production? In this role, you’ll work at the practical heart of scale-up: designing, building and commissioning a catalyst production pilot line, then using it to run tests, develop process knowledge and deliver new capable products to our production plants. Your work will also support production teams with troubleshooting and help plant engineering make informed equipment decisions.

Responsibilities

Your primary objective will be to deliver capable new catalyst products, supported by well-established and understood process windows, to the industrialization step—the next stage in our new product development stage-gate model.

You will plan and carry out work safely, optimize equipment and processes, report your findings, and document relevant best practices. You will also work with production and engineering colleagues to address equipment and process needs.

This will involve:

  • Designing, building and commissioning equipment for a catalyst production pilot line.
  • Performing tests at the Manufacturing Development Centre, including completing safety assessments and reporting results.
  • Troubleshooting production challenges and supporting problem-solving as a subject-matter expert in relevant unit operations and equipment.
  • Assisting plant engineering and EPCM with equipment selection, testing (on site or at vendors) and reviews.

What you will bring

  • Equipment and/or unit operation subject matter expert in e.g. powder handling, milling, screening, continuous furnaces etc.
  • Experience in Plant process engineering and commissioning experience
  • Minimum 7 -10 years of relevant experience
  • Experience troubleshooting and solving problems in industrial production processes.
  • A practical, hands-on approach and confidence working directly with equipment.
  • The ability to write clear, scientifically sound reports in English and communicate fluently in English, both spoken and written.
  • Flexibility to manage changing priorities and work to tight timelines.
  • Ability to work with several tasks and projects simultaneously, being robust/resilient when faced with challenges

It would also be an advantage to have:

  • Experience with production process scale-up or scale-down.
  • Danish, both written and spoken or with a willingness to learn the language
  • Project management experience.
  • Knowledge of risk assessment, data handling or statistics
  • Ability to think strategically and proactively seek information with respect to what is needed for future pilot development, Project manager experience, knowledge on risk assessment.
  • Knowledge on data handling and statistics an advantage

Why join us

You’ll have the opportunity to be a part of accelerating new catalyst products to the market by building and operating a pilot facility, take part in practical testing, optimizing, and solve real equipment and production challenges. The role brings together design, hands-on problem-solving and technical reporting, with work that supports scale-up and manufacturing development.

Your new Team

You’ll join R&D’s Scale-up and Manufacturing Development team. You’ll work with colleagues involved in developing and industrializing new catalyst products, pilot testing, production troubleshooting and plant engineering support. The team’s work connects equipment and process development with the needs of industrial production.

How you can apply:

If you would like to be part of a team of skilled and professional colleagues in an informal organization, please submit your documents in English.

Application deadline: 23-11-2026.

If you have questions regarding the role, feel free to reach out to Ninna Halberg Jokil, Director- Scale up and Manufacturing development, on NIH@topsoe.com.

You do not need to attach a cover letter to your application – just include a few sentences in your CV explaining why you are applying. Please also avoid the use of photos in your CV. Both these measures are to ensure a fair and unbiased process.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, irrespective of their gender, age, religion, disability, ethnic background, and geographical location. We encourage individuals from diverse cultures and countries to apply and contribute to our global team.

To ensure a secure and trustworthy work environment, our recruitment process may include background checks, requests for criminal records, and contact with references.

To headhunters: Thank you for your interest in our company. However, we would like to inform you that we have a dedicated internal team managing our recruitment process. We kindly request that you refrain from reaching out to us regarding potential candidates. Thank you for your understanding.

About us:

Topsoe is a leading global provider of advanced technology and solutions for the energy transition.

Built on decades of scientific research and innovation, we are working with customers and partners to drive energy resiliency and to achieve their sustainability goals.

We offer world-leading solutions for transforming renewable resources into fuels and chemicals, and we provide technologies needed to produce low-carbon and conventional fuels and chemicals as well as ensuring clean air.

We were founded in 1940 and are headquartered in Denmark, with around 2,500 employees serving customers all around the globe. To learn more, visit www.topsoe.com.

At Topsoe we strive towards having a safe work environment. We are aware of the risks in our work and continuously optimize our safety procedures.

​

title: SkillBridge HR Fellow
description:
Program Overview

Constellis is proud to participate in the Department of War (DoW) SkillBridge program, which provides transitioning service members with opportunities to gain valuable civilian work experience during their last 180 days of service. We are seeking a motivated and analytical Fellow to join our Human Resources team for a 12-week immersive training program.

This fellowship is designed to provide hands-on experience in core HR functions, including HR systems, data analytics, process improvement, and strategic business partnership. You will work alongside experienced HR professionals on real-world projects, gaining the practical skills and knowledge needed to launch a successful career in Human Resources.

Fellow Responsibilities

Throughout the 12-week program, you will:

  • Support HR Business Partners in compiling and analyzing workforce data, preparing dashboards, and identifying areas for process improvement.
  • Maintain and audit employee information in HR systems such as ADP and UKG.
  • Partner with the HR team to document workflows and streamline operational processes.
  • Participate in meetings and shadow HRBPs to understand how HR strategy supports business execution.
  • Complete the SHRM Essentials of Human Resources course to build a foundational understanding of HR laws, compliance, and best practices.
  • Develop and present a capstone analytics project on a key HR metric for leadership review.

What You Will Learn & Accomplish

This rotational program is structured to provide comprehensive exposure to the HR field:

  • Weeks 1-3: Orientation, HRBP role overview, and introduction to key HR systems (ADP, UKG) and data reporting.
  • Weeks 4-6: Foundational HR education, process documentation, and introduction to talent management cycles, FSLA, compensation, and job descriptions.
  • Weeks 7-9: Support engagement initiatives, project coordination, and cross-functional collaboration with Recruiting and Payroll.
  • Weeks 10-12: Execute an HR analytics project, develop presentation skills, and prepare a final program review for leadership.

Qualifications & Requirements

  • Active-duty U.S. Military service member within 180 days of separation and eligible for the DoW SkillBridge program.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • High proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel and PowerPoint.
  • A keen interest in human resources, systems, and data analysis.
  • Professional demeanor, curiosity, and a collaborative mindset.
  • No prior professional HR experience is required.

Program Benefits

  • Real-World Experience: Gain hands-on experience with industry-standard HR systems (ADP, UKG) and processes.
  • Professional Development: Complete the SHRM Essentials of HR course and receive mentorship from seasoned HR professionals.
  • Career Transition Support: Build your resume with tangible projects and receive guidance on post-military career planning in HR.
  • Networking: Connect with leaders and professionals across the Constellis organization.

description:

title: Program Manager
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Constellis is seeking a Program Manager to own its U.S. Army accounts and drive successful delivery of contracts supporting LEXSO (Layered Extended Security Operations), Constellis’ AI-enabled, open-architecture platform that fuses sensors, analytics, and decision engines into a single operating picture. This role combines program execution with business development: the Program Manager will grow the LEXSO Army portfolio by securing renewals and extensions, identifying new requirements across Army commands, and supporting capture and proposal efforts. The ideal candidate is a former Army officer with a technical engineering background and proven experience delivering AI, software, and analytics programs to Army customers in CONUS and OCONUS environments.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Serve as the single accountable owner for all assigned LEXSO Army accounts, managing the work scope, schedule, budget, and performance of each contract IAW approved Project Execution Plans, Company Directives, and department procedures
  • Drive successful delivery of Army programs, ensuring technical milestones, deliverables, and customer requirements are met within cost, schedule, and performance baselines
  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with Army customers, including senior leaders, program offices, contracting officer representatives (CORs), and end users across CONUS and OCONUS commands (e.g., U.S. Army Europe and Africa, U.S. Army Pacific)
  • Translate customer operational needs into LEXSO solution requirements, working with engineering and product teams to prioritize features, integrations, and deployments that deliver measurable mission value
  • Lead cross-functional delivery teams of engineers, data scientists, systems integrators, field technicians, and subcontractors; set priorities, resolve conflicts, and drive consensus among stakeholders
  • Grow the LEXSO Army portfolio by expanding work within existing accounts, securing contract renewals, extensions, and follow-on awards, and identifying new opportunities across Army organizations
  • Support business development and capture activities, including opportunity identification and qualification, customer shaping, pipeline management, and pricing and solution strategy
  • Manage or support proposal efforts in the role of Capture Manager and/or technical lead; author and review technical volumes, past performance, and pricing inputs for Army proposals
  • Represent LEXSO at Army industry days, conferences, demonstrations, and pilot deployments; communicate the LEXSO value proposition to technical and executive audiences
  • Manage program financials, including revenue, cost, margin, forecasts, and Estimate at Completion (EAC); work with Finance and Contracts to ensure compliance with FFP, T&M, and cost-type contract requirements
  • Prepare and conduct scheduled (typically monthly) program status briefings to the customer and Constellis leadership, explaining cost, schedule, and performance variances and corrective actions
  • Ensure all contract deliverables and reports (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly) are complete, accurate, and submitted on time and in the proper format
  • Identify and mitigate program risks and issues; implement process improvements that increase delivery efficiency and customer satisfaction
  • Provide oversight of subcontractors and technology partners assigned to the program
  • Develop organizational depth through mentoring, performance management, professional development, and succession planning
  • Ensure compliance with corporate policies, the Code of Business Ethics, applicable PSC.1 requirements, and the Security Operations Management System on all assigned programs
  • Other duties as assigned

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent is required
  • Active Secret security clearance with the ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret clearance
  • Minimum of 10 years of professional experience in program management, military operations, engineering, or defense technology delivery
  • Demonstrated experience owning an Army program portfolio valued at $10M or more, including securing renewals, extensions, or follow-on work
  • Experience leading cross-functional technical teams of 15 or more (e.g., engineers, data scientists, designers) and aligning product capabilities with customer and company objectives
  • Experience supporting proposals and capture efforts, including technical solutioning and proposal review
  • Working knowledge of program financials and contract types (FFP vs. T&M), including revenue, cost, and margin management
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to brief senior military and executive stakeholders
  • Decisive; able to navigate ambiguity and make sound business decisions with incomplete information and within compressed timelines
  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally, including OCONUS locations in Europe and the Indo-Pacific, up to 30%
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master’s degree in Business Administration (MBA), Engineering Management, or a related field
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license
  • Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification
  • Active Top Secret clearance
  • Prior service as a U.S. Army commissioned officer, including leadership, planning, or command-level experience
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification
  • Experience leading delivery of AI, software, data analytics, or other technology programs for U.S. Army or DoD customers
  • Experience with GenAI, sensor fusion, contested logistics, physical security, or counter-UAS (C-UAS) technologies
  • Experience supporting Army Europe and/or Indo-Pacific customers, including multinational exercises or partner-nation engagements
  • Experience managing engineering or construction contracts and multi-project portfolios
  • Familiarity with agile delivery and collaboration tools such as Jira, Confluence, and Asana

BENEFITS

Constellis offers a comprehensive, total rewards package that includes competitive compensation and a flexible benefits package that reflect its commitment to creating a diverse and supportive workplace.

WORKING CONDITIONS

Work is typically based in a busy office environment and subject to frequent interruptions. Business work hours are Monday-Friday standard core hours, however some extended or weekend hours may be required. This position requires regular travel to customer sites, including OCONUS locations, of up to 30%. Must be able to lift, lower, carry, push or move objects up to 25 lbs. Various tasks may require intermittent standing or prolonged sitting, and the ability to walk, reach, kneel, crouch and handle work related supplies and tools.

description:

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Monitor, identify, and assess potential insider threats, workplace violence concerns, security incidents, and suspicious activities that may impact personnel, facilities, operations, or organizational assets.

  • Investigate and evaluate indicators of concerning behavior, policy violations, fraud, theft, sabotage, espionage, or other insider threat activities.
  • Monitor criminal activity, protests, demonstrations, geopolitical developments, and other events that may present risks to personnel or operations.

  • Collaborate with security, investigations, human resources, legal, compliance, executive protection, crisis management, and operational teams to address identified threats and vulnerabilities.
  • Support incident response activities and provide analytical assistance during emerging security incidents.
  • Respond to high-priority intelligence requests and time-sensitive security matters.

QUALIFICATIONS

title: Records Technician
description:
POSITION: Records Technician

POSITION SUMMARY

This early career position supports case research, records analysis, financial reconciliation, and professional report preparation in a compliance-driven government contracting environment. The position requires strong written communication skills, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple assignments while meeting strict contractual standards.

The selected candidate will work with sensitive information and receive regular editorial feedback to ensure accuracy, clarity, and compliance.

RESPONSIBILITIES KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Case Research & Reporting

  • Conduct research and develop sources to complete assigned case leads.
  • Perform detailed record checks and verifications to ensure accuracy and contractual compliance.
  • Analyze discrepancies, resolve lead issues, and document findings.
  • Prepare clear, well-structured written summaries and investigative reports.
  • Revise written work based on editorial review and quality standards.

Financial & Administrative Support

  • Prepare and reconcile petty cash and escrow account transactions.
  • Process invoices, reconcile monthly credit card statements, and prepare payments for services.

Documentation & Workflow Management

  • Maintain organized documentation in accordance with internal policies and contract requirements.
  • Manage multiple active assignments at different stages while meeting deadlines.
  • Provide additional operational support as needed.
  • May be required to lift and carry awkward items weighing up to 25 lbs. Requires intermittent standing, walking, sitting, squatting, stretching and bending throughout the workday.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • U.S. Citizenship.
  • Minimum 18 years of age.
  • High School diploma or general education degree (GED).
  • Minimum of 2 years professional experience reviewing, analyzing, or summarizing documentation (any industry).
  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in a customer service or client-facing role demonstrating professionalism and responsiveness.
  • Strong written communication skills and the ability to produce clear, organized reports.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities in a deadline-driven environment.
  • High level of discretion when handling sensitive or confidential information.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to interpret written procedures and follow structured compliance guidelines.
  • Basic mathematical proficiency, including financial reconciliation and simple calculations.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and comfort working with databases and online research tools.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in investigative, legal, compliance, audit, or government-related environments.
  • Experience supporting government contracts or working within structured regulatory frameworks.
  • Familiarity with researching and navigating law enforcement, court, or archived records databases, including an understanding of jurisdictional distinctions and record accessibility.
  • Active Top Secret security clearance.

IMPORTANT APPLICANT INSTRUCTIONS

  • Provide a tailored resume reflecting relevant experience in records review, research, reporting, and multitasking.
  • To be considered, applicants must submit a writing sample (300 words or fewer) that demonstrates their ability to summarize information clearly and professionally.
  • Your writing sample should address:
    • Why you are interested in this role.
    • How your experience has prepared you to manage multiple assignments.
    • Your experience preparing written reports.
  • All submitted materials, including the writing sample, must be the applicant’s original work. The use of AI-generated or AI-assisted content is strictly prohibited, as AI tools are not permitted in the performance of this role.
  • Applications that do not include all required materials, exceed the stated length limits, or contain significant grammatical or formatting errors will not be considered. Attention to detail will be evaluated as part of the screening process.
