title: Project Manager
description:
1099 Independent Contractor | Charleston, South Carolina | Project-Based

Position Summary

Auro Hotels is seeking an experienced Project Manager – Independent Contractor to provide on-site Owner's Representative and construction management services for the Marriott Charleston Renovation in Charleston, South Carolina.

The project has completed the primary design phase and is transitioning into execution of the General Construction Contract. This position will be focused almost exclusively on construction execution, cost and schedule control, quality management, coordination with hotel operations, phased turnover, and project closeout.

This is a project-based 1099 independent contractor engagement requiring the Project Manager to be located in the Charleston market and available for a significant on-site presence throughout construction.

The Project Manager will serve as Auro Hotels' primary day-to-day project representative and will coordinate with the General Contractor, hotel operations, Marriott representatives, architects, interior designers, engineers, procurement teams, vendors, and other project stakeholders.

The primary objective is to deliver the renovation safely, on schedule, within the approved budget, and in accordance with the construction documents and Marriott requirements while minimizing disruption to the operating hotel.

Primary Responsibilities

General Contractor Management

  • Serve as Auro Hotels' primary day-to-day representative with the General Contractor.
  • Manage execution of the General Construction Contract and monitor compliance with contractual requirements.
  • Monitor GC staffing, subcontractor performance, sequencing, logistics, safety, quality, and overall execution.
  • Maintain an active presence in the field and conduct daily site walks.
  • Hold the GC accountable for schedule, cost, quality, documentation, and turnover requirements.
  • Review monthly applications for payment and verify reported completion against actual work in place.
  • Require corrective and recovery plans when performance or schedule milestones are at risk.

Schedule & Phasing

  • Manage the overall construction schedule with particular emphasis on guestroom renovation sequencing and phased turnover.
  • Review and challenge the GC's baseline schedule, monthly updates, three-week look-aheads, and recovery schedules.
  • Track critical-path and near-critical activities.
  • Coordinate construction sequencing with hotel occupancy and operations.
  • Manage floor and guestroom release dates between hotel operations and construction.
  • Coordinate utility shutdowns, noisy work, deliveries, freight elevator use, and other potentially disruptive activities.
  • Identify schedule risks early and drive resolution before they affect contractual milestones.

Budget & Cost Control

  • Maintain the Owner's construction budget and forecast through completion.
  • Review change-order requests, subcontractor proposals, allowances, unit pricing, and supporting documentation.
  • Evaluate proposed changes for scope validity, quantity, labor, materials, markups, schedule impacts, and contractual entitlement.
  • Negotiate or assist in negotiating change orders on behalf of the Owner.
  • Maintain current change-order, potential-change, allowance, and contingency logs.
  • Identify cost exposures before they become committed costs.
  • Review GC payment applications and provide recommendations for approval.
  • Maintain an accurate forecast of anticipated final construction cost.

Field Construction & Quality Control

  • Maintain a consistent on-site presence throughout active construction.
  • Verify work conforms to the contract documents, approved submittals, Marriott requirements, and approved mock-ups.
  • Identify deficient or unacceptable work early and require corrective action.
  • Coordinate resolution of field conditions with the GC, architect, interior designer, engineers, and Owner.
  • Monitor quality of guestrooms, bathrooms, corridors, public spaces, meeting areas, F&B spaces, and other renovated areas.
  • Monitor protection of existing hotel finishes and operational areas adjacent to construction.
  • Coordinate punch-list inspections and verify completion prior to Owner acceptance.

RFI, Submittal & Document Management

  • Monitor RFIs, submittals, shop drawings, samples, substitutions, and design clarifications.
  • Identify overdue decisions or approvals that could affect construction or procurement.
  • Coordinate responses among the GC, consultants, Marriott, hotel operations, and Owner.
  • Maintain organized records of project correspondence, meeting minutes, field reports, approvals, changes, and photographs.

FF&E / Owner-Furnished Item Coordination

  • Coordinate construction with Owner-procured FF&E, OS&E, signage, artwork, technology, and specialty equipment.
  • Confirm rough-ins, blocking, backing, electrical requirements, dimensions, and installation conditions are coordinated before finishes are completed.
  • Coordinate delivery schedules with procurement and logistics teams.
  • Confirm areas are ready before FF&E deliveries and installations.
  • Coordinate GC trades with FF&E installers.
  • Track missing, damaged, delayed, or incorrect items affecting room and area turnover.

Operating Hotel Coordination

The Marriott Charleston will remain an operating hotel during significant portions of the renovation. Coordination with hotel operations will therefore be a critical responsibility.

The Project Manager will:

  • Maintain regular communication with the General Manager and appropriate department heads.
  • Coordinate guestrooms and floors being removed from and returned to inventory.
  • Manage construction access and separation from guests and hotel employees.
  • Coordinate temporary barriers, signage, dust control, noise restrictions, and life-safety requirements.
  • Coordinate loading dock, freight elevator, staging, storage, and worker access.
  • Plan disruptive activities around hotel occupancy, group business, meetings, events, and other operational requirements.
  • Minimize impacts to guest experience and hotel revenue wherever reasonably possible.

Meetings & Reporting

  • Lead or participate in weekly Owner/Architect/Contractor meetings.
  • Conduct focused schedule, cost, procurement, and operational meetings as required.
  • Provide concise weekly reporting covering construction progress, schedule, budget, change orders, RFIs, procurement, FF&E, quality, operational impacts, risks, and required Owner decisions.
  • Immediately escalate significant cost, schedule, quality, safety, or operational issues.

Turnover & Closeout

  • Develop and manage phased turnover procedures for guestrooms and public areas.
  • Coordinate GC, design team, Marriott, hotel operations, housekeeping, engineering, IT, security, and FF&E inspections.
  • Manage punch-list development, assignment, completion, and verification.
  • Confirm guestrooms and renovated areas are fully complete before release back to hotel operations.
  • Coordinate testing, commissioning, demonstrations, and training.
  • Manage warranties, attic stock, spare materials, O&M manuals, as-built drawings, permits, inspections, and other closeout documentation.
  • Track completion of warranty and post-turnover deficiencies.
  • Assist with final payment and release of retainage.

Required Project Controls

The Project Manager will maintain or actively manage:

  • Master project schedule
  • Three-week look-ahead schedule
  • Construction budget and forecast
  • Change-order and potential-change logs
  • Contingency and allowance logs
  • RFI and submittal logs
  • Procurement / long-lead log
  • FF&E delivery and installation schedule
  • Owner decision log
  • Punch-list / deficiency log
  • Guestroom turnover matrix
  • Risk and issue log
  • Payment application tracking

Qualifications

  • Minimum 5–8 years of commercial construction/project management experience.
  • Hotel renovation experience required.
  • Experience executing renovations within an occupied and operating hotel required.
  • Marriott or comparable major full-service hotel brand experience preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of construction means, methods, sequencing, scheduling, and contract administration.
  • Strong capabilities in construction cost management, change-order review, RFIs, submittals, payment applications, and forecasting.
  • Ability to read and interpret architectural, interior design, structural, MEP, and life-safety documents.
  • Experience coordinating FF&E procurement and installation with construction.
  • Proficiency with Excel, Bluebeam, scheduling software, and construction/project-management platforms.
  • Strong communication, documentation, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.

Location & Engagement Requirements

  • This position is a 1099 independent contractor engagement for the Marriott Charleston Renovation project.
  • The Project Manager must be located in the Charleston, South Carolina market for the duration of the assignment.
  • A significant and consistent on-site presence at the Marriott Charleston is required during active construction.
  • This is not intended to be a remote project-management assignment.
  • The contractor must be available to respond to time-sensitive field, operational, schedule, and construction issues as they arise.
  • The engagement is anticipated to continue through construction, phased turnover, final completion, and project closeout.

Engagement Terms

  • Contract Duration: This is a project-based 1099 independent contractor engagement with an anticipated duration of approximately 14 months, generally corresponding with the active construction, phased turnover, and closeout of the Marriott Charleston Renovation.
  • Potential for Additional Assignments: Successful completion of this engagement may lead to additional project opportunities with Auro Hotels in the Charleston market. Any future assignments would be subject to project needs and separate agreement between Auro Hotels and the contractor.
  • On-Site Commitment: The Project Manager will be required to maintain a minimum of 30 hours per week on site at the Marriott Charleston during active construction. The position requires flexibility based on construction activities, hotel operations, critical milestones, and project needs.
  • Weekend Availability: Construction activities, shutdowns, guestroom turnovers, inspections, and other project requirements may occasionally require weekend or off-hours presence. The Project Manager will be expected to coordinate their schedule accordingly when project conditions require it.
  • Charleston Market Requirement: The selected individual must be based in the Charleston, South Carolina market for the duration of the engagement and able to respond promptly to time-sensitive project and field conditions.
  • Independent Contractor Status: The Project Manager will perform services as an independent contractor and will be responsible for their own normal business and daily living expenses, taxes, insurance, and other obligations associated with independent contractor status, except for specifically approved reimbursable project expenses.
  • Reimbursable Expenses: Reasonable and necessary business expenses incurred specifically at the request of Auro Hotels and outside the contractor's normal daily living and local commuting expenses will be eligible for reimbursement, subject to Auro Hotels' approval and applicable expense policies. Examples may include company-directed travel to Auro Hotels' Greenville Company Resource Center, approved project-related travel outside the Charleston market, lodging associated with approved business travel, and other specifically authorized project expenses.
  • Expense Reporting: The contractor will submit a monthly reimbursable expense report with appropriate receipts and supporting documentation for eligible expenses. Normal meals, local commuting, housing, personal vehicle expenses, and other ordinary costs associated with living and working in the Charleston market will not be considered reimbursable unless specifically authorized in advance by Auro Hotels.
  • Compensation: Compensation will be established as a fixed monthly independent contractor fee, payable in accordance with the executed consulting/independent contractor agreement. Approved reimbursable expenses will be paid separately and will not be considered part of the contractor's monthly fee.
  • Project Completion: The engagement is expected to continue through construction, phased guestroom and public-area turnover, final completion, punch-list resolution, and project closeout. The specific commencement and completion dates will be established in the final independent contractor agreement.

Measures of Success

Performance will be evaluated based on:

  • Completion within the approved project budget.
  • Achievement of construction and operational milestone dates.
  • Timely turnover of guestrooms and revenue-producing areas.
  • Effective management of change orders and Owner contingency.
  • Quality of completed construction.
  • Minimal disruption to hotel guests and operations.
  • Timely identification and resolution of field issues.
  • Successful Owner and Marriott inspections.
  • Complete and timely project closeout.

The successful candidate will be a field-oriented Project Manager who takes ownership of execution, anticipates issues before they affect the project, and is comfortable holding contractors and consultants accountable for their contractual responsibilities.

title: Material Analyst
description:
Smith Industries is the leading fabricator of oil and gas surface production equipment in West Texas and Eastern New Mexico. Since 2004, we've provided design engineering, drafting, procurement, fabrication, and modular construction to operators across the Permian Basin.

The Material Analyst makes sure every piece of material that comes into the shop is the right material, properly documented, and traceable to the job it goes on, for both ASME pressure parts and structural steel. Reporting to the Supply Chain Manager, this position works closely with Purchasing, Quality Control, and Production to keep receiving current, MTRs reviewed and filed, and work orders ready to pass inspection and ship on time.

Essential Duties:

  • Receive incoming material the same day it arrives, matching it to the PO and packing list, recording heat numbers and quantities, and tagging material
  • Document over, short, and damaged (OS&D) shipments and notify Purchasing and Production
  • Review MTRs and certificates of conformance against the PO, drawing, and applicable codes (ASME II and VIII, ASTM, AWS D1.1), verifying grade, size, and heat number
  • File MTRs by work order and work down the MTR backlog while keeping current receiving caught up daily
  • Track shortages by PO, vendor, ETA, and owner, and follow up with vendors on missing material, MTRs, and certifications until closed
  • Check BOMs and cut lists against stock and open POs one to two weeks ahead of production, and track remnants by heat number
  • Verify databooks for upcoming shipments are complete, with every MTR present and matched
  • Keep the ERP system, MTR tracker, and receiving log accurate, with no duplicates, blanks, or missing counts
  • Use company-approved AI tools to pull data from MTRs, compare MTRs to POs, check logs for errors, and draft vendor follow-ups and reports, verifying all output against the source documents
  • Prepare daily reports on MTRs processed, backlog remaining, receiving status, and open issues
  • Perform cycle counts and support month-end backlog, receiving, and shortage reporting
  • Follow all safety policies, wear required PPE, and report all incidents immediately; stop work when a job cannot be done safely
  • Other duties as assigned
Requirements

  • 2+ years of experience in materials, receiving, inventory, or QC documentation in a manufacturing or fabrication environment
  • Ability to read an MTR and match grade, size, heat number, and spec to a PO and drawing
  • Ability to work in the yard with required PPE and lift up to 50 lbs
Experience and Education

  • High school diploma or equivalent experience
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience with an ERP or inventory system
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools such as ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, or Claude for document and data work
  • Knowledge of ASME, ASTM, AWS, and AISC standards; pressure vessel or structural fabrication experience preferred
  • Familiarity with common materials such as SA-516-70, SA-106B, SA-105, A36, A572-50, A992, and A500 preferred
  • Ability to read drawings and BOMs; forklift certification a plus
Skills and Abilities

  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy in documentation and data entry
  • Organized, with a habit of following up on open items until they are closed
  • Able to balance daily receiving and backlog work and deliver quality work on tight timeframes
  • Professional written and verbal communication and strong interpersonal skills
  • Sound judgment and decision-making with the company's best interests in mind
Benefits

Full-time employees are eligible for:

  • Competitive pay
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Paid time off and paid holidays
  • Life and disability insurance

title: Senior Python Engineer
description:
In this role, you will take full ownership of our core Django service, which acts as the main bridge between our algorithmic models and internal teams. You’ll be responsible for API design, data modeling, cross-team data contracts, and maintaining high performance at scale. As part of the Algo Development team reporting to the Engineering Manager, you will also productionize research code and mentor a junior engineer. We are open to Senior and Staff levels, with the final title agreed upon during the process.

- Bachelor’s/Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent hands-on experience.

- 7+ years of commercial software engineering experience with a primary focus on Python and running production-grade services (excluding internal tools, scripts, or prototype notebooks; Staff candidates are expected to have a longer track record).

- Extensive production experience with Django and Django REST Framework (DRF), including shipping, scaling, and troubleshooting complex services (handling high-traffic ORM N+1 queries, transaction boundaries, migrations under load, and custom querysets).

- Build & scale Django services: Design, deploy, and maintain high-load Django and Django REST Framework applications on PostgreSQL, ensuring clean data modeling, robust API design, and schema consistency across multiple domains.

- Optimize PostgreSQL & manage Auth: Analyze query execution plans, build effective indexes, and tune performance (including time-series via TimescaleDB and spatial queries via PostGIS). Implement enterprise authentication solutions: OAuth/OIDC, federated SSO, token validation, and identity provider integrations.

- Set up Wagtail CMS from scratch: Architect and build the partner and operator CMS ground-up, defining page models, structured content, media workflows, and the authoring interface.

- Productionize research & algorithms: Wrap research models into production microservices with strict data contracts, model versioning, reliable REST endpoints, and complete observability.

- Guide architecture & mentor: Lead code reviews, define foundational architecture patterns, and mentor a junior Python engineer to elevate team standards.

Benefits

- 20 days of paid vacation, 5 sick days.

- Flexible schedule with a high level of autonomy.

- Opportunity to influence product and technical decisions.

- Professional growth and learning opportunities.

- Comfortable working environment with a supportive team.

title: Bodily Injury Claims Representative

title: Full-Stack Software Engineer
description:
Job Description

Job Description

Position Purpose:

The Software Engineer leads full-stack software development for medical In Vitro Diagnostic (IVD) devices and provides software engineering support for biological analysis software packages. This role bridges low-level hardware interaction and high-level user interfaces, developing robust software applications, configuring operating system environments, and verifying code against established regulatory and technical specifications. The engineer will design and build intuitive UI/UX for non-technical users to control complex scientific instruments, interface directly with microcontrollers and embedded hardware, and enable automated analysis of complex biological datasets to provide actionable information to end users.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Lead full-stack software development efforts for medical IVD systems and biological analysis software, spanning lower-level microcontroller/hardware interfaces to upper-level application logic and user interfaces.
  • Design, build, and refine intuitive graphical user interfaces (UI/UX) that enable scientific personnel and non-technical operators to control analytical instruments and sensor networks.
  • Program, integrate, and test low-level microcontrollers (e.g., Arduino or similar platforms) to communicate with biological sensors, custom boards, and peripherals.
  • Write, test, and optimize high-performance C++ codebases as well as Python applications for instrumentation control, data processing, and analytical workflows.
  • Implement cybersecurity controls, software hardening procedures, and secure coding practices within production and operational environments.
  • Adhere to quality management system (QMS) protocols and regulatory/ISO standards (e.g., ISO 13485, ISO 62304) throughout the software development lifecycle, including formal design controls, risk assessments, and code documentation.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams—including biologists, systems engineers, hardware developers, and project leads—to translate technical wireframes and scientific requirements into production-ready software.
  • Troubleshoot and debug complex hardware/software integration issues, recreating user workflows to isolate root causes and optimize operating efficiency.
  • Author and maintain software lifecycle documentation, design specifications, verification/validation protocols, and end-user operating manuals.

Required Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • C++ Expertise: Strong software development experience in modern C++ for application and hardware-adjacent logic.
  • Microcontrollers & Hardware Interfacing: Demonstrated experience working with microcontrollers (e.g., Arduino, ARM, or microprocessors) and hardware communication protocols.
  • UI/UX Design: Proven ability to create user-centered, intuitive GUIs and desktop/embedded interface experiences.
  • Python (Highly Preferred): Proficiency in Python for scripting, backend application logic, data science pipelines, or test automation.
  • Full-Stack Development: Solid understanding of full-stack system architecture, connecting frontend user interfaces through backend processing to low-level device drivers and hardware.
  • ISO & Regulatory Compliance (Preferred): Familiarity or prior experience working within ISO quality frameworks (e.g., ISO 13485, ISO 62304, ISO 9001, or equivalent regulated industry standards, with med-tech experience strongly preferred).
  • Cybersecurity (Preferred): Knowledge of cybersecurity controls, system security procedures, secure boot/data handling, and vulnerability mitigation in production software.
  • Production Environments: Experience building, deploying, and maintaining software in commercial production environments.
  • Operating Systems & Tools: Experience with Linux environments, custom board configurations, version control (Git), and issue tracking systems (Jira).
  • Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills: Diagnostic and debugging capabilities for complex hardware-software-data integrations.
  • Java and other coding languages/frameworks (Optional): Additional familiarity with other languages is a plus.

Education/Experience:

  • BS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering with a software focus, or equivalent technical degree.
  • 3 to 5 years of professional software engineering experience.
  • Prior experience in medical devices (IVD), biotechnology, or scientific analytical instrumentation software development is strongly preferred..

Clearance:

  • This position requires that the candidate be willing and able to complete a successful background screening for a security clearance. Candidates with a current security clearance will receive preference.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • N/A

Working Conditions / Equipment:

  • This is a full-time, on-site position with flexible work arrangements. This position primarily operates during standard business hours, with occasional needs for extended workdays or weekend work to meet project timelines. The role may also require infrequent domestic travel for conferences, trade shows, or research-related meetings. The ability to lift and carry light loads (under 25 lbs) without assistance is necessary.
